<p align="justify" style="margin: 0px; clear: left; font-family: 'times new roman'; font-size: 10pt;"><font style="font-family: 'times new roman', times; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</font></p><p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: center;"><font style="color: #000000;"><a style="text-decoration: none; color: #000000; cursor: default; outline: none;" href="#" name="1_HN0W3SSCV4G80KGW80G84WCSWKW8WG" class="customBookmark"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 12pt; font-weight: bold;"><font style="text-decoration: underline;">PART<font style="color: #000000; text-decoration: underline;"> I</font></font></font></a></font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: center;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt;"><font style="text-decoration: underline;"><font style="color: #000000;"><a style="text-decoration: none; color: #000000; cursor: default; outline: none;" href="#" name="2_PMEKPJUE3KK8SSCGO4SKWSKWCCWS4O" class="customBookmark"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 12pt; font-weight: bold;">Item <font class=" FactMarked">1</font>. Business.</font></a></font></font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-style: italic; font-weight: bold;">Unless the context requires otherwise, references in this Form 10-K to &#8220;MGC&#8221; or &#8220;MGC Diagnostics&#8221; mean MGC Diagnostics Corporation, while references to &#8220;Medical Graphics&#8221; refer to Medical Graphics Corporation, a wholly-owned subsidiary of MGC Diagnostics Corporation and references to &#8220;Medisoft&#8221; refer to Medisoft SA, a wholly-owned subsidiary of MGC Diagnostics Corporation, and its subsidiaries. MGC Diagnostics, Medical Graphics and Medisoft are collectively referred to as the &#8220;Company.&#8221;</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-weight: bold;">Overview</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt; text-indent: 34.2pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">MGC Diagnostics Corporation (the &#8220;Company&#8221;) is a global medical technology company dedicated to cardiorespiratory health solutions. The Company designs, markets and sells non-invasive cardiorespiratory diagnostic products through its Medical Graphics Corporation subsidiary under the MGC Diagnostics brand and trade name and through its Medisoft subsidiary under the Medisoft brand and trade name. MGC acquired Medisoft on August 1, 2014. The Company&#8217;s product portfolio provides solutions for disease detection, integrated care, and wellness across the cardiorespiratory healthcare spectrum. The Company sells its products internationally through distributors and in the United States through a direct sales force targeting specialists located in hospitals, university-based medical centers, medical clinics, physician offices, pharmaceutical companies, medical device manufacturers, and clinical research organizations (&#8220;CROs&#8221;). The Company&#8217;s cardiorespiratory diagnostic products measure flow and respiratory pressures and, in most cases analyze the inhaled and exhaled gases such as oxygen and carbon dioxide. The Company operates in a single industry segment: the research, development, manufacture and marketing of non-invasive cardiorespiratory diagnostic products.</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt; text-indent: 34.2pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">The Company had revenues of $<font class=" FactMarked">40.0</font> million and operating loss&nbsp;of $<font class=" FactMarked">2.6</font> million for the year ended October 31, 2016. &nbsp;The operating loss included several&nbsp;significant items, including:</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;"><br></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;"> (i) charges of $3.3 million and $0.3 for impairment of goodwill and certain intangible assets, respectively, recorded upon&nbsp;the acquisition of Medisoft in fiscal 2014;</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;"><br></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">(ii)&nbsp;$1.0 million of combined charges for legal settlement costs and obsolete inventory related to the Company's 2014 strategic initiative to enter the sleep diagnostics market; and </font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;"><br></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">(iii) $0.7 million&nbsp;of charges for impairment of excess inventory related to the Company's strategic initiatives to distribute the Resmon PRO FOT device.</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;"><br></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">Domestic product sales and service revenue accounted for 77% of fiscal <font class=" FactMarked">2016</font> revenue and&nbsp;international product sales accounted for the remaining 23%. Revenue consists of equipment, supply and accessory sales as well as service revenue. Equipment, supply and accessory sales reflect sales of non-invasive cardiorespiratory diagnostic equipment and aftermarket sales of peripherals, software, supplies and additional training. Service revenue consists of revenues from extended service contracts and non-warranty services.</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-weight: bold;">General</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">MGC Diagnostics designs and markets non-invasive cardiorespiratory diagnostic products that have a wide range of applications within cardiorespiratory healthcare.</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">Healthcare professionals use cardiorespiratory diagnostic products to assess the cause and degree of severity for shortness of breath and lung diseases such as asthma, emphysema and bronchitis (each are forms of Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease or &#8220;COPD&#8221;), and to manage related treatment. Through breath-by-breath analysis, some of the Company&#8217;s cardiorespiratory diagnostic products measure the level of disability and functional capacity to help physicians diagnose and treat heart diseases such as heart failure and coronary disease. The Company also sells its cardiorespiratory diagnostic products and services to clinical research customers for use in drug and device clinical trials both in the United States and internationally. Other health professionals use the Company&#8217;s cardiorespiratory diagnostic products to measure calorie consumption and to prescribe safe and effective exercise in rehabilitation, obesity management, general fitness, and athletic performance. These applications operate by measuring air flow and the concentrations of inhaled and exhaled gases such as oxygen and carbon dioxide while a person is at rest, or exercising on a bike or treadmill. This assessment of gases and air flow can also be used to determine nutritional requirements of critically ill patients in a hospital intensive care unit (&#8220;ICU&#8221;) and cardiac catheterization laboratory.</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;">&nbsp;<br></p>

<p style="margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">Primary products for each of Medical Graphics and Medisoft include pulmonary function (&#8220;PFT&#8221;) and gas exchange (&#8220;GX&#8221;) testing products, as discussed below in &#8220;Pulmonary Function Products&#8221; and &#8220;Gas Exchange Testing Products.&#8221; All MGC Diagnostics products are designed to be simple and easy to use while providing the flexibility to address specific needs of hospitals, clinics and physician offices. MGC Diagnostics&#8217; products, except for some original equipment manufacturer (&#8220;OEM&#8221;) components, are generally sold with a personal computer, color monitor, printer and other peripherals. These products increasingly include networked and internet&nbsp;technologies that offer remote processing applications and communications.</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt;"><br></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-weight: bold;">Seasonality</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">The Company experiences some seasonality in its revenues, with the fourth quarter of its fiscal year traditionally being its strongest quarter. The Company experiences variability in the other <font class=" FactMarked">three</font> quarters <font class=" FactMarked">due</font> to a number of factors, including customer budget cycles, product introductions, Company sales incentive programs, general economic conditions and the timing of customer orders. See &#8220;Management&#8217;s Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations-Seasonality.&#8221;</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-weight: bold;">Pulmonary Function Products</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">Pulmonary function testing (PFT) equipment and techniques have come into widespread use and standardization over the past <font class=" FactMarked">30</font> years. Advances in computer technology and miniaturization have aided in the development of devices that have become portable and user-friendly through sophisticated software.</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">Health care professionals use diagnostic pulmonary function assessment to diagnose lung diseases such as asthma or COPD; </font><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">the majority of assessments are performed for diagnostic purposes or to monitor patient response to therapy. Pulmonary function testing is an important tool in the management of respiratory diseases including asthma, chronic bronchitis, cystic fibrosis, emphysema, and restrictive pulmonary disease, among others. The majority of pulmonary function assessments are performed on patients with suspected pulmonary disease; however, there are non-pulmonary applications for cardiology, chemotherapy and neuromuscular analysis. </font><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">Pulmonary function applications range from (i) basic lung function screening, to (ii) pre-operative surgical evaluations and post-operative assessment of heart and lung transplant patients, to (iii) disability assessment from occupational exposures, and to (iv) documenting</font><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;"> responses to a variety of therapies.</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">These pulmonary function products fall into <font class=" FactMarked">four</font> major product categories: (i) Spirometry, (ii) Complete Pulmonary Function, (iii) Body Plethysmography and (iv) Specialty Products.</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;"><br></p>
<table cellspacing="0" cellpadding="0" style="border-collapse: collapse; margin-left: 0pt; width: 100%;" width="100%">

<tr>
<td style="vertical-align: top; width: 3%;">
<p style="margin: 0pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;"> &nbsp; </font></p>
</td>

<p style="margin: 0pt;"><font style="font-family: Symbol; font-size: 10pt;"> &#61623; </font></p>
</td>
<td style="vertical-align: top; width: 95%;">
<p style="margin: 0pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-style: italic; font-weight: bold;"> Spirometry. </font><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">Spirometry is a relatively simple, painless, and inexpensive method of assessing pulmonary function. In this procedure, the patient breathes into a spirometer, an instrument that measures and records (i) the volume of exhaled or &#8220;expired&#8221; air and (ii) the airflow rate for a specific time period. Spirometry provides measurement, lung capacity and mechanical properties of airflow. </font><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;"><font class=" FactMarked">Due</font> to the simplicity of testing and the availability of portable equipment, spirometry is widely used in both inpatient and outpatient settings. MGC Diagnostics markets the <strong>Medical Graphics CPF S/D USB<sup>TM</sup></strong> and the <strong>Medisoft Micro <font class=" FactMarked">5000</font></strong> and <strong>Micro <font class=" FactMarked">6000</font></strong> spirometers. The spirometer is a product platform that can be upgraded to complete a pulmonary function or cardiopulmonary exercise system. </font></p>
</td>

</td>
<td style="vertical-align: top; width: 95%;">
<p style="margin: 0pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-style: italic; font-weight: bold;"> Complete Pulmonary Function. </font><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">Pulmonary function testing equipment measures and analyzes breathing to evaluate the condition of the heart, lungs, and metabolism. The technique is used to diagnose and manage numerous pulmonary conditions. Although diagnostic spirometry is adequate for basic pulmonary function screening, complete pulmonary function analysis is required to diagnose the specific cause of lung disease. MGC Diagnostics markets <strong>Medical Graphics Ultima PF Series<sup>TM</sup></strong>, <strong>Medisoft SpiroAir</strong> and <strong>Medisoft HypAir</strong> as complete pulmonary function systems. These complete pulmonary function systems, available as a desktop or cart-mounted configuration, perform spirometry, non-invasive measurement of an individual&#8217;s total lung capacity, respiratory mechanics and diffusing capacity, and the oxygen transfer across the lungs into and out of the bloodstream. In fiscal 2016, the Company received Federal Drug Administration approval for the <strong>Resmon PRO FOT</strong> (Forced Oscillation&nbsp;Technique) device, adding to this range of equipment.</font></p>

<p style="margin: 0pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-style: italic; font-weight: bold;"> Body Plethysmograph. </font><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">Body plethysmographs consist of an airtight, transparent patient cabin, an adjustable support arm, pressure transducers for measuring mouth and cabin pressure and a computer. Many devices also incorporate diffusing capacity and lung volume by nitrogen washout, which enhances the scope of use. The patient sits inside the enclosure and undergoes diagnostic pulmonary function tests. MGC Diagnostics markets the <strong>Medical Graphics Platinum Elite</strong> and the <strong>Medisoft BodyBox Series</strong>, each of which are designed to minimize patient anxiety and discomfort while maximizing accuracy. These systems&#8217; designs optimize patient comfort within a clear-view acrylic enclosure and allow testing of a broad population, including pediatric patients and individuals in wheelchairs.</font><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-style: italic;"> </font></p>

<p style="margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">MGC Diagnostics&#8217; pulmonary function products&#8217; ease of us</font><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">e, infection control features, compact, lightweight design, connectivity and mobility options attract a wide variety of customers, including pulmonary laboratories in hospitals, clinics, physician offices, occupational medicine clinics, asthma/allergy practices, and clinical research centers worldwide.</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-weight: bold;">Gas Exchange Testing Products</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">MGC Diagnostics&#8217; cardiopulmonary exercise (&#8220;CPX&#8221; or &#8220;CPET&#8221;) testing products measure functional capacity, fitness or conditioning levels, evaluate prognostic criteria for surgical procedures as well as help physicians diagnose heart and lung diseases. Cardiopulmonary exercise testing provides objective, reliable, and quantitative assessment of the cardiovascular and respiratory responses to varying external workloads. These products operate by measuring the volume of air and concentrations of oxygen and carbon dioxide as they enter and leave the lungs while an individual exercises on a machine such as a bike or treadmill. These tests may be augmented by various types of monitoring, including electrocardiogram (&#8220;ECG&#8221;), blood pressure, and pulse oximetry.</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">Cardiopulmonary exercise testing is useful (i) to differentiate between cardiac and pulmonary problems, (ii) to diagnose exercise-induced asthma, (iii) to assess preoperative risk, (iv) to determine disability and response to therapeutic interventions, (v) to determine the functional status in heart failure, and (vi) to develop exercise programs.</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">MGC Diagnostics products can also perform measurements of individuals at rest to determine nutritional requirements of critically ill patients or individuals wishing to assess the number of calories burned per day, which is termed &#8220;energy expenditure.&#8221; This measurement is known as a &#8220;metabolic assessment&#8221; and is marketed by the Company as the indirect calorimetry option for many of its gas exchange products. Configurations combining the cardiopulmonary exercise testing, energy expenditure and pulmonary function applications are marketed under both MGC Diagnostics&#8217; Medical Graphics and M</font><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">edisoft products.</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">The Medical Graphics </font><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-weight: bold;">Ultima Series</font><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;"> is sold in the following different configurations</font><font style="color: #0000ff; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-weight: bold;">:</font></p>

<p style="margin: 0pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-weight: bold;">Cycle Ergometers and Treadmills</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">The Company offers several models of exercise devices that provide healthcare professionals and patients a tool for improved diagnosis and more successful outcomes in clinical rehabilitation. A cycle ergometer is a specially-designed stationary exercise bicycle that can operate at a broad spectrum of resistance levels while a treadmill is a motorized walking/running surface that can operate at different inclines to produce a range of work levels. These ergometers and treadmills can be used and controlled by the Company&#8217;s cardiopulmonary exercise testing products.</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">Through MGC Diagnostics&#8217; Medical Graphics business, the Company sells non-proprietary cycle ergometers and treadmills manufactured by best-in-class industry partners used in diagnostic, rehabilitation and sports medicine applications. Through MGC Diagnostics&#8217; Medisoft business, the Company manufactures and sells <font class=" FactMarked">three</font> models of treadmills &#8211; the </font><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-weight: bold;">Clinical <font class=" FactMarked">870</font>A, Sport <font class=" FactMarked">870</font>S </font><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">and </font><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-weight: bold;">Athlete <font class=" FactMarked">870</font>C</font><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-style: italic; font-weight: bold;">.</font></p>
<p align="justify" style="margin: 0px; clear: left; font-family: 'times new roman'; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;&nbsp;</p>
<p style="margin: 0pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-weight: bold;">Electronic Medical Records Interfaces</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">Both Medical Graphics and Medisoft sell HL<font class=" FactMarked">7</font> interface technology software, installation and support for data communication interfaces to achieve interoperability between the Company&#8217;s products and the electronic medical records systems used in hospital and clinical settings. Electronic medical record systems are designed to facilitate more complete, rapid transmission of patient and test results between the patient care management systems and equipment. These patient information&nbsp;management systems are intended to improve quality of care and reduce operating costs through improved accuracy, timeliness and efficiency of records management.</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-weight: bold;">Competition</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">The industry for companies selling cardiorespiratory diagnostic products is mature and competitive. There are a number of companies that currently offer, or are in the process of developing, products that compete with products offered by MGC Diagnostics. The Company&#8217;s competitors include both large and small medical companies, some of which have greater financial and technical resources and broader product lines. Vyaire&nbsp;(a successor&nbsp;to the former CareFusion Respiratory Solutions entity), nSpire Health, Cosmed, Ganshorn, ndd and Morgan Scientific are the Company&#8217;s principal competitors. &nbsp;Morgan Scientific markets select Medisoft hardware&nbsp;within the United States. The Company believes that the primary competitive factors in its markets are product features, customer service, price, quality, product performance, market reputation, breadth of product offerings and effectiveness of sales and marketing efforts. The Company believes that its product quality, product performance, market reputation and customer service are true differentiators that will contribute to future growth.</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<div class="pageBreak">
<table style="width: 100%;" width="100%">

<tr>
<td class="pgno" style="padding: 0px; text-align: center;"><font style="font-size: 10pt;" class="pageno"><font class='pageno'>7</font></font></td>

<div style="page-break-before: always; font-size: 10pt; text-align: left;"><font style="font-family: 'times new roman', times; font-size: 10pt;"><a href="#TOC">Table of Contents</a></font></div>
</div>
<p style="margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;"><br></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">The Company believes price competition will continue to be an important factor in customer purchasing patterns as a result of healthcare cost containment pressures in both the domestic and international health care industry. Domestically, a number of industry participants and associations increasingly rely on group purchasing organizations (&#8220;GPOs&#8221;) in the effort to contain healthcare costs. The Company became a qualified provider for several of the larger domestic GPOs to ensure the Company&#8217;s continued access to its market and to efficiently increase its sales to the expanded numbers of companies using these buying groups. Our relationship with these GPOs is continuing and can provide MGC with additional exposure to customers whose relationships with the GPO precluded past relationships with them. As the numbers of purchasers aligning with these GPOs have increased, the percentage of Company revenues attributable to GPO sales has increased as well.</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">Any product developed by the Company that gains regulatory approval must compete for market acceptance and market share. The timing of market introduction of competitive products could adversely affect the competitiveness of the Company&#8217;s products. Accordingly, the relative speeds with which the Company can develop products, complete clinical testing and the regulatory approval process and supply commercial quantities of the product to the market are important competitive factors. The Company expects that competition will also be based on many factors, including device size and weight, longevity, ease of programmability, ability to provide diagnostic capability, product reliability, physician familiarity with the device, patent protection, sales and marketing capability, third-party reimbursement policies, reputation and price. The Company has protected its products with various patents and trademarks when possible.</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-weight: bold;">Manufacturing</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">MGC&#8217;s Medical Graphics subsidiary currently designs and assembles all major sensor components of its cardiopulmonary diagnostic products including its data acquisition systems, flow measurement sensors, gas sample lines, gas chromatograph, nitrogen, carbon dioxide, oxygen and other gas analyzers. The Company purchases Medical Graphics-designed sheet metal, electrical components, printed circuit boards and some measurement devices from outside vendors and these components are tested, assembled and packaged by Medical Graphics personnel into fully integrated systems.</font></p>
<p align="justify" style="margin: 0px; clear: left; font-family: 'times new roman'; font-size: 10pt;"><br></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">MGC&#8217;s Medisoft subsidiary currently designs, fabricates and assembles most&nbsp;major sensor components of its cardiopulmonary diagnostic products including its data acquisition systems, flow measurement sensors, gas sample lines, nitrogen, carbon dioxide, oxygen and other gas analyzers. Medisoft designs and fabricates sheet metal, electrical components, and printed circuit boards at its Belgium facility. Medisoft purchases some measurement devices from outside vendors; Medisoft personnel then test, assemble and package these components into fully integrated systems.</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">The Company also acquires general-purpose computers, monitors and printers from a variety of sources and integrates its proprietary software modules into these products. Medical Graphics acquires its cycle ergometers and treadmills from third parties, while Medisoft manufactures its treadmills and acquires ergometers from third parties.</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">The Company&#8217;s Quality Management System is certified to the requirements of ISO <font class=" FactMarked">13485</font>:<font class=" FactMarked">2003</font>, Canadian Medical Device Regulations Part <font class=" FactMarked">1</font>, and European Union Medical Device Directive Annex II regarding the Development and Production of Cardiorespiratory devices. See &#8220;Foreign Government Regulation.&#8221; below for additional discussion of the Company&#8217;s ISO <font class=" FactMarked">13485</font>:<font class=" FactMarked">2003</font> certification.</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-weight: bold;">Marketing and Distribution</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">MGC Diagnostics&#8217; Medical Graphics subsidiary markets its products in the United States through its direct sales force that sells into hospitals, university-based medical centers, medical clinics, physician offices, pharmaceutical companies, medical device manufacturers and clinical research organizations. Medical Graphics markets its products to a wide range of customers that use its products and services across a broad market continuum. Each Medical Graphics domestic salesperson is responsible for a specific geographic area and is compensated with a base salary, expense reimbursement and a sales commission plan.</font></p>

International revenues accounted for <font class=" FactMarked">12.8</font>% and <font class=" FactMarked">17.7</font>% of total Medical Graphics revenue for the years ended October 31, 2016 and <font class=" FactMarked">2015</font>, respectively. Medisoft markets its products to a wide range of customers that use its products and services across a broad market continuum.</font><br><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

These distributors typically carry a select inventory of Medisoft products and sell those products in specific geographic areas, generally on an exclusive basis. Revenues outside of Belgium accounted for 88.9% of total Medisoft revenue for fiscal <font class=" FactMarked">2016</font>. <p style="margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">International sales involve certain risks not ordinarily associated with domestic business, including fluctuations in the purchasing power of local currencies, reliance on distributors and country-specific policies and procedures. Medical Graphics sells all its products on a dollar-denominated basis while Medisoft sells all its products on a Euro-dominated basis. As a result, although neither subsidiary has direct exposure to currency exchange rates risk, changes in exchange rates affect the relative competitiveness of the Company&#8217;s products and services in various markets.</font></p>

<p style="margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">MGC Diagnostics executes multiple sales and marketing strategies both domestically and internationally. The Company&#8217;s most successful sales and marketing tactics include product demonstrations that emphasize technological capabilities and advantages, breadth of services and unmatched customer support. In addition to on-site product demonstrations, the Company annually attends and hosts booth displays at various industry-specific meetings and trade shows around the world. At these events, potential customers/clients have the ability to see and experience the unique features our products offer. Through these global events, the Company gains exposure to pulmonologists, cardiologists, respiratory therapists, allergy physicians, exercise physiologists, sports medicine professionals, personal trainers and exercise enthusiasts.</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;"><br></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;"><font style="background-color: #ffffff;">Other Company marketing initiatives include educational seminars, print advertisements, direct mail, telemarketing and e-marketing ca</font>mpaigns through its websites </font><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; text-decoration: underline;">www.mgcdiagnostics.com </font><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">and </font><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; text-decoration: underline;">www.medisoft.be</font><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">. Group Purchasing Organizations (&#8220;GPOs&#8221;) have become increasingly present in our market as hospitals work to streamline their supply chain. Vendors can become accredited by the GPOs, which can facilitate the selling process. The Company has a relationship with all major GPOs, including Amerinet, HealthTrust, Premier Purchasing, Vizient, and the Government Services Administration (&#8220;GSA&#8221;). Sales associated with GPO relationships were $<font class=" FactMarked">20.5</font>&nbsp;million and $<font class=" FactMarked">16.1</font>&nbsp;million in fiscal <font class=" FactMarked">2016</font>&nbsp;and <font class=" FactMarked">2015</font>, respectively.</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-weight: bold;">Research and Development</font></p>

The Company&#8217;s research and development initiatives are targeted for hospitals, clinics and physician&#8217;s offices. An integral component of the Company&#8217;s future growth strategy is the development and introduction of additional new products and complementary software.</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

See Item <font class=" FactMarked">7</font>, Management&#8217;s Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations-Research and Development.</font></p>

<p style="margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-weight: bold;">Intellectual Property</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-weight: bold;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">Patents and trademarks are critical in the medical device industry. The Company believes strongly in protecting its intellectual property and has a long history of obtaining patents, when available, in connection with its research and product development programs. The Company also relies upon trade secrets and proprietary know-how.</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">The Company relies on a combination of patent, trademark and trade secret laws to establish proprietary rights in its products. The Company's&nbsp;Medical Graphics subsidiary currently h</font><font style="font-size: 10pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman';"><font style="font-family: 'times new roman', times;">olds six&nbsp;United States</font></font><font style="color: #0000ff; font-family: 'times new roman', times; font-weight: bold;"> </font><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman';"><font style="font-family: 'times new roman', times;">pate</font></font></font><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">nts (with various expirations between 2026 and 2031), with one&nbsp;patent pending and a number of foreign patents with respect to technologies covered by its United States patents. These patents collectively cover the various aspects of MGC Diagnostics&#8217; core technologies, ranging from gas analysis, pressure and flow measurement to methods of analyzing cardiorespiratory data and expert system software. The Company's&nbsp;Medisoft subsidiary currently has two&nbsp;patents pending covering diagnostic technologies used in its product</font><font style="font-size: 10pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman';"><font style="font-family: 'times new roman', times;">s.&nbsp;</font></font><font style="font-family: 'times new roman', times;">United States patents filed on or after June 8, 1995 have a term of <font class=" FactMarked">20</font> years from the date on which the patent application was filed.</font></font></p>
<p align="justify" style="margin: 0px; clear: left; font-family: 'times new roman'; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</p>
<p style="margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">Foreign patents generally expire <font class=" FactMarked">20</font> years after the date of original application, but vary from country to country. MGC Diagnostics intends to aggressively enforce its intellectual property rights and has successfully done so in the past. We cannot ensure, however, that these patents, or any patents that may be issued as a result of existing or future applications, will offer any degree of protection from competitors.</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">MGC Diagnostics&#8217; Medical Graphics subsidiary also owns registered trademarks and has applied for other trademarks in the U.S. and certain foreign countries. MGC Diagnostics owns and actively enforces an array of related copyrights and trademarks. These include: </font><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-weight: bold;">BreezeConnect&#8482; HL<font class=" FactMarked">7</font> interface</font><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;"> </font><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-weight: bold;">technology, BreezeSuite WebReview&#8482; physician review software, Platinum Elite&#8482; body plethysmograph, RTD&#8482; real-time diffusion, Ultima&#8482; CardiO<font class=" FactMarked">2</font>&#174; gas exchange analysis system, Ultima CPX&#8482; metabolic stress testing system and Ultima PF&#8482; pulmonary function system</font><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">, as well as various logos.</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">Although patent and intellectual property disputes in the medical device industry have often been settled through licensing agreements or similar arrangements, costs associated with these arrangements may be substantial and we cannot ensure that necessary licenses would be available to the Company on satisfactory terms, if at all. Accordingly, an adverse determination in a judicial or administrative proceeding or failure to obtain necessary licenses could prevent the Company from manufacturing and selling its products, which would have a material adverse effect on the Company&#8217;s business, financial condition and results of operation.</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">The Company seeks to protect its trade secrets and proprietary intellectual property, including know-how, in part, through confidentiality agreements, non-compete agreements and assignment of invention provisions in agreements with employees, consultants and other parties, as well as through contractual exclusivity with certain suppliers. We cannot ensure, however, that these agreements will not be breached, that the Company would have adequate remedies for any breach, or that the Company&#8217;s trade secrets will not otherwise become known to or independently developed by competitors.</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">The Company conducts ongoing evaluations of potential infringement of any proprietary rights of third parties by the products the Company intends to market. Regardless of the Company&#8217;s efforts to evaluate the potential infringement of any proprietary rights of third parties, we cannot ensure that such infringements do not exist or may not arise in the future. There has been substantial litigation regarding patent and other intellectual property rights in the medical device industry. Litigation, which could result in substantial cost to and diversion of effort by the Company, may be necessary to enforce patents issued to or licensed by the Company, to protect trade secrets or know-how owned by the Company, to defend the Company against claimed infringement of the rights of others and to determine the scope and validity of the proprietary rights of others. Adverse determinations in litigation could subject the Company to significant liabilities to third parties or could require the Company to seek licenses from third parties.</font></p>
<div class="pageBreak">&nbsp;<br></div>
<p style="margin: 0pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-weight: bold;">Government Regulation.</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-weight: bold;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-style: italic; font-weight: bold;">United States Government Regulations.</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt;">&nbsp;</p>
<p style="margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">Most of the products manufactured by the MGC Diagnostics&#8217; Medical Graphics subsidiary are &#8220;devices&#8221; as defined in the Federal Food, Drug and Cosmetic Act (the &#8220;Act&#8221;) and are subject to the regulatory authority of the Food and Drug Administration (&#8220;FDA&#8221;), which regulates the manufacture, distribution, related record keeping, labeling and advertising of these devices. The FDA classifies medical devices in commercial distribution into <font class=" FactMarked">one</font> of <font class=" FactMarked">three</font> classes, Class I, II or III, following the enactment of the Medical Device Amendments to the Act in May 1976 (the &#8220;Amendments&#8221;). These classifications are based on the controls necessary to reasonably ensure the safety and efficacy of medical devices.</font></p>
<p align="justify" style="margin: 0px; clear: left; font-family: 'times new roman'; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</p>
<div class="pageBreak">
<div class=" ParaMarked">
<table style="width: 100%;" width="100%">

<tr>
<td class="pgno" style="padding: 0px; text-align: center;"><font style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'times new roman', times;" class="pageno"><font class='pageno'>10</font></font></td>
</tr>

</table>
</div>
<hr style="border-bottom-color: #000000; border-top-color: #000000; color: #000000; background-color: #000000;"></hr>
<div style="page-break-before: always; font-size: 10pt; text-align: left;"><font style="font-family: 'times new roman', times; font-size: 10pt;"><a href="#TOC">Table of Contents</a></font></div>
</div>
<p align="justify" style="margin: 0px; clear: left; font-family: 'times new roman'; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</p>
<p style="margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">Many Class I devices have been exempted from pre-market notification requirements by the FDA. The same types of controls the FDA has used on devices since the passage of the Act in <font class=" FactMarked">1938</font> can adequately regulate these products. These &#8220;general controls&#8221; include provisions related to labeling, producer registration, defect notification, records and reports and good manufacturing practices. The more comprehensive Quality System Regulation (&#8220;QSR&#8221;) has replaced the good manufacturing practice regulation. As noted below, QSRs include implementation of quality assurance programs, written manufacturing specifications and processing procedures, written distribution procedures and record keeping requirements.</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">Class II devices are products for which the general controls of Class I devices are deemed not sufficient to ensure the safety and effectiveness of the device and thus require special controls. Special controls for Class II devices include performance standards, post-market surveillance, patient registries and the use of FDA guidelines. Standards may include both design and performance requirements.</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">Class III devices have the most restrictive controls and require pre-market approval by the FDA. Generally, Class III devices are limited to life-sustaining, life-supporting or implantable devices.</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">All of MGC Diagnostics&#8217; Medical Graphics products are Class II devices.</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">If the Company does not comply with applicable regulatory requirements, including marketing products only for approved uses, it could be subject to fines, injunctions, civil penalties, recall or seizure of products, total or partial suspension of production, refusal of the government to grant pre-market clearance or pre-market approval for products, withdrawal of approvals and criminal prosecution. In addition, changes in existing regulations or adoption of new governmental regulations or policies could prevent or delay regulatory approval of the Company&#8217;s products or result in increased regulatory costs. Furthermore, once clearance or approval is granted, subsequent modifications to the approved product or manufacturing process may require a new round of clearances or approvals that could require substantial additional clinical data and FDA review.</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">As Class II devices, the Company&#8217;s domestic sales of its registered devices became taxable when the Health Care and Education Reconciliation Act of <font class=" FactMarked">2010</font> (in conjunction with the Patient Protection and Affordable Care Act, Public Law <font class=" FactMarked">111</font>-<font class=" FactMarked">152</font>) added section <font class=" FactMarked">4191</font>, </font><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-style: italic;">Medical Devices</font><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;"> for sales subsequent to December 31, 2012. This excise tax is levied at a rate of <font class=" FactMarked">2.3</font>% of the relevant sales price of the products. Effective January 1, 2016, and ending on December 31, 2017, The Consolidated Appropriations Act, <font class=" FactMarked">2016</font>, signed into law on December 18, 2015, included a <font class=" FactMarked">two</font>-year moratorium on the medical device excise tax. Currently legislation is being drafted in both the House of Representatives and Senate to permanently repeal the tax, which if passed is expected to be signed into law by the new administration.</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-style: italic; font-weight: bold;">Class II Requirements.</font><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;"> Section <font class=" FactMarked">510</font>(k) of the Act requires individuals or companies manufacturing medical devices intended for use with humans to file a notice (&#8220;<font class=" FactMarked">510</font>(k) Notification&#8221;) with the FDA at least <font class=" FactMarked">90</font> days before introducing a product not exempted from notification requirements into the marketplace. The <font class=" FactMarked">510</font>(k) Notification must state the class in which the device is classified and the action taken to comply with performance standards or pre-market approval that may be needed if the device is a Class II or Class III device, respectively. Under Section <font class=" FactMarked">510</font>(k), a medical device can be marketed if the FDA determines that the device is substantially equivalent to similar devices marketed prior to May 28, 1976. In the past, Medical Graphics has filed notifications with the FDA of its intent to market its products pursuant to Section <font class=" FactMarked">510</font>(k) of the Amendments. The FDA subsequently cleared these products for commercial sale and Medical Graphics is now marketing the devices under Section <font class=" FactMarked">510</font>(k). The FDA action does not, however, constitute FDA approval of the Company&#8217;s products or pass upon their safety and effectiveness.</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">In addition to the requirements described above, the Act requires that all medical device manufacturers and distributors register with the FDA annually and provide the FDA with a list of those medical devices that they distribute commercially. The Act also requires that all manufacturers of medical devices comply with applicable labeling requirements, including Unique Device Identification ("UDI") requirements when applicable, and manufacture devices in accordance with QSRs, which require that companies manufacture their products and maintain their documents in a prescribed manner with respect to manufacturing, testing and quality control.</font></p>
<p align="justify" style="margin: 0px; clear: left; font-family: 'times new roman'; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</p>
<div class="pageBreak">
<div class=" ParaMarked">
<table style="width: 100%;" width="100%">

<tr>
<td class="pgno" style="padding: 0px; text-align: center;"><font style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'times new roman', times;" class="pageno"><font class='pageno'>11</font></font></td>
</tr>

</table>
</div>
<hr style="border-bottom-color: #000000; border-top-color: #000000; color: #000000; background-color: #000000;"></hr>
<div style="page-break-before: always; font-size: 10pt; text-align: left;"><font style="font-family: 'times new roman', times; font-size: 10pt;"><a href="#TOC">Table of Contents</a></font></div>
</div>
<p style="margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">In addition, these manufacturers are subject to inspection on a routine basis for compliance with the QSRs. The FDA&#8217;s Medical Device Reporting regulation requires that companies provide information to the FDA on death or serious injuries alleged to have been associated with the use of their products, as well as product malfunctions that would likely cause or contribute to death or serious injury if the malfunction were to recur. The FDA further requires that certain medical devices not cleared with the FDA for marketing in the United States meet specific requirements before they are exported. The FDA has authority to inspect the Company&#8217;s facilities to ensure compliance with the Act and regulations thereunder. Failure to comply with these regulations could have a material adverse effect on the Company&#8217;s business, financial condition and results of operations. Medical Graphics is registered as a manufacturer with the FDA and successfully passed its most recent FDA inspection</font><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-weight: bold;"> </font><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">in June 2015.</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-style: italic; font-weight: bold;">Foreign Government Regulation.</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">The Company&#8217;s products and processes are also subject to regulation similar to that of the FDA in various foreign countries. ISO <font class=" FactMarked">13485</font>:<font class=" FactMarked">2003</font> certification indicates that a company&#8217;s development and manufacturing processes comply with standards for quality assurance and manufacturing process control. CE Certification evidences a company&#8217;s compliance with the requirements of the European Medical Device Directive <font class=" FactMarked">93</font>/<font class=" FactMarked">42</font>/EEC and allows it to affix the &#8220;CE Mark&#8221; to its products. The CE Mark denotes conformity with the applicable European standards for safety and allows CE marked devices to be placed on the market in all European Union (&#8220;EU&#8221;) countries. Since June 1998, medical devices cannot be sold in EU countries unless they display the CE Mark. MGC Diagnostics&#8217; Medical Graphics subsidiary received ISO <font class=" FactMarked">13485</font> certification for its development and manufacturing processes in <font class=" FactMarked">1998</font> and has passed annual surveillance and recertification audits, the most recent of which occurred in June 2016. Medisoft also is ISO <font class=" FactMarked">13485</font> certified. Medical Graphics and Medisoft have achieved CE certification for its primary cardiopulmonary testing products. We cannot ensure, however, that Medical Graphics or Medisoft will be able to obtain regulatory approvals or clearances for our products in foreign countries. In addition to compliance with the ISO <font class=" FactMarked">13485</font> Quality System standard, Medical Graphics&#8217; and Medisoft&#8217;s products and Quality Systems also meet Part I of the Medical Device Requirements for Canada and have obtained device licenses from Health Canada.</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-weight: bold;">Employees</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-weight: bold;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">As of January 16, 2017, the Company had <font class=" FactMarked">155</font>&nbsp;full-time employees (114&nbsp;in Medical Graphics and 41&nbsp;in Medisoft). No employees are represented by a collective bargaining agreement and the Company has not experienced any work stoppage. Management believes that relations with its employees are good.</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

Austin is a globally recognized clinical and medical device industry expert and leader with extensive experience, spanning more than <font class=" FactMarked">20</font> years, in product development and marketing, strategic planning, business development, profit and loss&nbsp;responsibility, and clinical consulting.</font></p>

From July 2006 to September 2010, Austin was Director of Marketing for CareFusion (now Vyaire), a leading, global health care company, where his responsibilities included overall marketing operations for respiratory diagnostic products supporting global sales in excess of $<font class=" FactMarked">200</font> million annually, while coordinating product launch planning for more than <font class=" FactMarked">10</font> global markets. Austin holds a Bachelor of Science degree from Mount Marty College.</font></p>

Risk Factors.</font></a></font></font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-style: italic; font-weight: bold;">Our resu<font>lts are affected by changes in worldwide economic and capital markets conditions. </font></font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;"><font><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">We derived <font class=" FactMarked">23.5</font>% and <font class=" FactMarked">28.1</font>% of our respective fiscal <font class=" FactMarked">2016</font>&nbsp;and <font class=" FactMarked">2015</font>&nbsp;revenues from outside the United States. Our business may be adversely affected by factors in the United States and other countries that are beyond our control, such as downturns in economic activity or labor conditions in a specific country or region.</font></font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt;"><font><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-style: italic; font-weight: bold;">Our ownership and operation of Medisoft entails ownership of Euro-denominated assets, liabilities, revenues and expenses and Dollar-Euro currency changes have adversely affected our results.</font></font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;"><font><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">We incurred foreign currency losses of $<font class=" FactMarked">46,000</font> and $<font class=" FactMarked">929,000</font> in fiscal <font class=" FactMarked">2016</font>&nbsp;and <font class=" FactMarked">2015</font>, respectively. In the same <font class=" FactMarked">two</font> years, we also incurred foreign currency translation gains (losses) of $<font class=" FactMarked">22,000</font> and $(<font class=" FactMarked">149,000</font>), which&nbsp;are reflected in accumulated other comprehensive loss in our consolidated balance sheet. Our business may be adversely affected by Euro and other currency rate fluctuations against the US Dollar.</font>&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt;"><font><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-style: italic; font-weight: bold;">If we are unable to attain synergies from the acquisition of Medisoft, our sustained profitability may be uncertain.</font></font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;"><font>We have made significant p</font>ersonnel and financial resource commitments for the acquisition and integration of Medisoft. Medisoft incurred losses of $4,510,000 and $<font class=" FactMarked">999,000</font> in fiscal 2016 and&nbsp;<font class=" FactMarked">2015</font>, respectively. If we are unable to generate revenue growth and operational synergies from our continued efforts, our combined profitability and financial position may continue to be adversely affected.</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-style: italic; font-weight: bold;">We own significant inventory of a product&nbsp;that we are selling into the U.S. market for the first time, since only recently receiving FDA clearance.</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">We have entered into a distribution agreement under which we agreed to purchase and resell third-party products in markets that are adjacent to our core cardiorespiratory diagnostic products. </font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">In <font class=" FactMarked">2012</font>, we entered into an agreement with a European company under which we purchased&nbsp;forced oscillation technique&nbsp;(&#8220;FOT&#8217;) products for resale. As of October 31, 2016, we had FOT inventory with a carrying value of $0.5 million, after incurring impairment charges of $0.7 million in fiscal 2016 results. We have&nbsp;clearance to sell this product in Europe and&nbsp;we received FDA clearance to market and sell this product in the United States late in calendar year 2016, but we cannot ensure that we will be able to market and sell all of the units&nbsp;currently on hand. Although the FOT product is now authorized for sale in a number of countries, if we do not achieve sales levels sufficient to realize the carrying value&nbsp;of this inventory or if we are unable to extend or renew our contract to distribute this product with the manufacturer, we may be required to take an additional impairment charge against this inventory.</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-style: italic; font-weight: bold;">We are engaged in the orderly disposal&nbsp;of a sleep diagnostic product.</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">In March 2014, we entered into an agreement with Neurovirtual USA, Inc. (&#8220;Neurovirtual&#8221;) under which we agreed to purchase and sell Neurovirtual sleep diagnostics products. At October 31, 2016, we had an inventory of</font><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-style: italic;"> </font><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">Neurovirtual sleep diagnostic products with a carrying value&nbsp;of $<font class=" FactMarked">0.2</font>&nbsp;million after incurring impairment charges of $0.3 million as of October 31, 2016.&nbsp;</font><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">On June 14, 2016, we settled litigation with Neurovirtual that resulted in the termination of the agreement&nbsp;and allowed us to continue selling this inventory, under full warranty according to the termination&nbsp;agreement. </font><font style="font-family: 'times new roman', times; font-size: 10pt;">If we are unable to successfully resell the remaining inventory,&nbsp;we may&nbsp;be required to record an additional impairment charge against any remaining inventory.</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0in 0in 0.0001pt; font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', serif;"><b><i><font style="font-size: 10.0pt;">Failure to achieve and maintain effective internal controls could limit our ability to detect and prevent fraud and thereby adversely affect our business and stock price.</font></i></b><font style="font-size: 10.0pt;"></font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0in 0in 0.0001pt; text-indent: 0.5in; font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', serif;"><font style="font-family: 'times new roman', times;"><font style="font-size: 10.0pt;" class="selected">Effective internal controls are necessary for us to provide reliable financial reports. Nevertheless, all internal control systems, no matter how well designed, have inherent limitations. Even those systems determined to be effective can provide only reasonable assurance with respect to the consolidated financial statement preparation and presentation. Our inability to maintain an effective control environment may cause investors to lose confidence in our reported financial information, which could in turn have a material adverse effect on our stock price. The Company, while reviewing its internal controls noted a material weakness. See Item 9A for further details.</font></font></p>
