<p style="margin: 0pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-style: italic; font-weight: bold;">We have commenced litigation against the Medisoft selling shareholders. </font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;"><font><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">In November 2015, we commenced litigation in the French-speaking courts of Brussels, Belgium against the Medisoft selling shareholders for violations of representations and warranties in the stock purchase agreement dated as of July 10, 2014 under which we purchased Medisoft. We alleged that these violations resul</font><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">ted in damages to us of approximately &#8364;<font class=" FactMarked">985,400</font> ($<font class=" FactMarked">1,084,000</font>). In May 2015, we received payment of &#8364;<font class=" FactMarked">406,700</font> ($<font class=" FactMarked">447,000</font>) with respect to these alleged violations pursuant to a bank-guaranteed contractual escrow fund and we have reflected that payment on our bo</font><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">oks and records. On May 30, 2016, the&nbsp;defendant selling shareholders&nbsp;filed an answer and asserted a counterclaim against us seeking to recover the &#8364;406,700 that was paid plus legal costs. We continue to believe the Medisoft selling shareholders are liable to us for violations of representations and warranties&nbsp;in the stock purchase agreement&nbsp;and continue to pursue this matter. We have not accrued any losses related to the litigation and have not accrued any related legal costs that we have not yet incurred. We expect that this litigation process in the Belgian courts may continue until the fall of <font class=" FactMarked">2017</font>.&nbsp;<font style="font-family: 'times new roman', times;"> Although we believe our claims against the Medisoft selling shareholders have merit, litigation is uncertain and can be expensive, particularly in a foreign jurisdiction.<font style="mso-spacerun: yes;">&nbsp; </font>We cannot ensure that we will recover additional amounts against the Medisoft selling shareholders, and if we are unsuccessful, we may be required to return a portion of the payment we received.<font style="mso-spacerun: yes;">&nbsp; </font>See Part I, Item 3 Legal Proceedings. </font></font></font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt;"><font><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</font></font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt;"><font><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-style: italic; font-weight: bold;">We have capitalized significant costs and expenses related to new software products. </font></font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt;"><font><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 5pt;">&nbsp;</font></font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;"><font><font><font style="font-family: 'times new roman', times; font-size: 10pt;" class="selected">We capitalize costs to develop new software products because these software products are an integral part of our diagnostic medical devices. We begin to capitalize costs related to new software development products once we have achieved technological feasibility and we have completed all research and development for the product&#8217;s components. We amortize these software costs on a straight-line basis over the estimated useful life of the related product beginning when the product is available for general customer release. See &#8220;Intangible Assets, Note <font class=" FactMarked">7</font> of Notes to Financial Statements.&#8221;</font></font></font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt;"><font><font><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</font></font></font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;"><font><font><font style="font-family: 'times new roman', times; font-size: 10pt;"><font class="selected"><font style="background-color: #ffffff;" class="selected">At October 31, 2016, we had net book value for capitalized software development costs of $<font class=" FactMarked">3.3</font>&nbsp;million, most</font>&nbsp;of which is related to a new operating software platform for our cardiorespiratory diagnostic products that has not been placed into service. During fiscal <font class=" FactMarked">2016</font>, we capitalized an additional $0.7 million&nbsp;of software development costs. During fiscal <font class=" FactMarked">2016</font>, we determined that another in-service&nbsp;software product was impaired and incurred a $<font class=" FactMarked">0.2</font>&nbsp;million impairment charge. If we determine that any software is impaired in the future, then we will be required to incur a charge against earnings in the amount of the impaired software.&nbsp; We will be&nbsp;submitting a Traditional 510(k) application through an accredited Third Party Reviewer&nbsp;to the FDA for clearance to introduce our new software platform to the market in fiscal 2017. If the FDA delays clearance on our&nbsp;new operating software platform&nbsp;for any reason, thereby delaying our ability to introduce this software in the market, it could have a material adverse effect on our operations, including affecting our future revenues and the carrying value of this software.</font></font></font></font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 5pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-style: italic; font-weight: bold;">Our success depends on our ability to sell our Medical Graphics and Medisoft cardiorespiratory products into our core hospital, clinic and physician office markets.</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;"><font style="font-family: 'times new roman', times; background-color: #ffffff; color: #000000; font-size: 10pt;">Our current succes<font>s depends on our ability to successfully upgrade existing accounts with new products and services, convert competitive accounts and provide billable and warranty services. Our longer term success depends on our ability to sustain new product developments, re</font>tain existing customers and increase our global market share.</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-style: italic; font-weight: bold;">Our association with domestic Group Purchasing Organizations (&#8220;GPOs&#8221;) may result in reduced gross margins.</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 5pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">Group Purchasing Organizations ("GPOs") are entities through which groups of end-customers of a product act together through an agent to purchase a product from a distributer, supplier or manufacturer. GPOs operate routinely in the healthcare market. Price competition or negotiated lower prices with GPOs may exert downward pressure on prices we are able to charge for our products. We cannot ensure that we will be able to offset any downward price pressure through corresponding cost reductions. Any failure to offset this pressure could have an adverse effect on our business, results of operations and financial condition.</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-style: italic; font-weight: bold;">Healthcare policy changes, including national legislation to reform the U.S. healthcare system, may have a material adverse effect on our business.</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">There have been and continue to be proposals by the federal government, state governments, regulators and third-party payers to control healthcare costs and, more generally, to reform the U.S. healthcare system. The Patient Protection and Affordable Care Act imposed a <font class=" FactMarked">2.3</font>% excise tax on all U.S. medical device sales beginning in calendar <font class=" FactMarked">2013</font>. This tax adversely affected our profitability. Although this tax has been suspended for <font class=" FactMarked">two</font> years beginning January 1, 2016, it may be imposed again in the future after the period of suspension ends. &nbsp;Additionally, if the market reduces purchase commitments during the period of uncertainty that may arise due to the recent change in government administration, we could experience a flattening or reduction in sales during this period. We are also unsure of the effect on the U.S. healthcare system of the new administration that took office on January 20, 2017.</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

</div>
<p style="margin: 0pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-style: italic; font-weight: bold;">If we are unable to sustain profitability in <font class=" FactMarked">2017</font>&nbsp;and beyond, our liquidity may be adversely affected. </font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">Although we were profitable in fiscal <font class=" FactMarked">2013</font> and <font style="border-left: none; border-right: none;"><font class=" FactMarked">2015</font></font>, we were unprofitable in fiscal <font class=" FactMarked">2008</font> through <font class=" FactMarked">2012</font> and in fiscal <font class=" FactMarked">2014</font> and 2016 and had an accumulated deficit of $<font class=" FactMarked">8.1</font>&nbsp;million as of October 31, 2016. While we believe that our existing cash balance of $<font class=" FactMarked">7.27</font>&nbsp;million as of October 31, 2016 is adequate to support operations for at least the next fiscal year, even after giving effect to the cash dividend we will pay in February 2017, we must sustain profitability. If this is not possible, we may need to obtain additional financing to be able to meet our future cash flow requirements, and we cannot ensure that we will be able to obtain such financing on terms favorable to us or at all.</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-style: italic; font-weight: bold;">The financial stability of our vendors could affect our business and results of operations. </font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">We rely on third party vendors for certain components used in our products. We purchase a number of significant components, such as capacitors, batteries and integrated circuits, from sole source suppliers. Although we attempt to maintain sufficient quantities of inventory of these components to minimize production delays or interruptions, we cannot ensure that we will find suitable alternatives at reasonable prices, if at all, or that any alternatives will remain available to us. Our inability to obtain acceptable components in a timely manner or find and maintain suitable replacement suppliers for components would have a material adverse effect on us, including our ability to manufacture our products. As a result of the disruptions in the financial markets and other macro-economic challenges currently affecting the economy of the United States and other parts of the world in recent years, our vendors may have experienced and continue to experience cash flow concerns. As a result, vendors may increase their prices, reduce their output or change terms of sales. Any demands by vendors for different payment terms may adversely affect our earnings and cash flow.</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt; line-height: 1;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-style: italic; font-weight: bold;">Technology in the medical device industry changes rapidly.</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">Rapid technological change, changing customer needs and frequent new product introductions are all characteristics of the medical device industry. We face intense competition from other device manufacturers that may have access to greater resources. Our products may be rendered obsolete as a result of future innovations. Our competitors may succeed in obtaining regulatory approval and introducing products before we do. Any of these developments could have a significant negative impact on our business and results of operations.</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt; line-height: 1;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-style: italic; font-weight: bold;">Our future operations are dependent upon variables outside our control. </font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">Successful implementation of our business plan depends on the interaction of many variables, including the effects of changing industry conditions and new competition. While we believe that our business plan reflects reasonable judgments in assessing those risks, we cannot ensure that unforeseen influences will not adversely affect our ability to execute our business plan strategies. While we believe that our business plan projections are in line with achievable performance levels, we cannot ensure that we will be able to obtain, and sustain, projected sales revenue.</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt; line-height: 1;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-style: italic; font-weight: bold;">Protection of intellectual property is critical to our business.</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">Patents and trademarks are critical in the medical device industry. We believe strongly in protecting our intellectual property and have a long history of obtaining patents, when available, in connection with our research and product development programs. We own a number of United States and foreign patents. We also own registered trademarks, and have applied for other trademarks in the United States and foreign countries. We cannot ensure that we will be granted patents and trademarks in the future, or that any patents and trademarks that we now hold or may be granted, or under which we have held license rights, will be valid or otherwise be of value to us. Even if our patents and trademarks are valid, others may be able to introduce non-infringing competitive products.</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">Although patent and intellectual property disputes in the medical device area have often been settled through licensing agreements or similar arrangements, costs associated with these arrangements may be substantial, and we cannot ensure that necessary licenses would be available to us on satisfactory terms or at all. Accordingly, an adverse determination in a judicial or administrative proceeding or failure to obtain necessary licenses could prevent us from manufacturing and selling our products, which would have a material adverse effect on our business, financial condition and results of operations.</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">We seek to protect our trade secrets and proprietary intellectual property, including know-how, in part, through confidentiality agreements, non-compete agreements and assignment of invention provisions in agreements with employees, consultants and other parties, as well as through contractual exclusivity with certain suppliers. We cannot ensure that these agreements will not be breached, that we would have adequate remedies for any breach, or that our trade secrets will not otherwise become known to or independently developed by competitors.</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin: 0pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt; line-height: 1;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-style: italic; font-weight: bold;">Realization of our deferred tax assets depends on our continued profitability.</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">Our current profitability in the U.S. and our expectation of future profitability in U.S. and Belgian operations is the basis for our&nbsp;valuation allowance on domestic and foreign deferred tax assets. The valuation of the respective deferred tax assets of Medical Graphics and Medisoft depends on the respective future profitability of each company. Our inability to achieve necessary levels of profitability could require us to record valuation reserves&nbsp;against our recorded deferred tax assets.</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt; line-height: 1;"><font><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-style: italic; font-weight: bold;" class="selected">We cannot guarantee that we will pay future dividends</font><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-weight: bold;">.</font></font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;"><font style="font-family: 'times new roman', times; font-size: 10pt;"><font><font>We r</font>ecently declared a special dividend.<font style="mso-spacerun: yes;">&nbsp; </font>The fact that we declared a special dividend does not suggest and shareholders should not expect that our Board of Directors will declare a regular or special cash dividend in the future. Any future dividends wi</font>ll depend on a variety of factors including, our liquidity and balance sheet position, solvency, strength of operations, product successes, research and development needs and other factors.</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 5pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt; line-height: 1;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-style: italic; font-weight: bold;">We depend upon our senior management and other key personnel</font><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-weight: bold;">.</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">Our success depends largely on effective leadership from our senior management and other key personnel. Competition for qualified personnel with sufficient and relevant experience in the medical device industry is intense. Accordingly, the loss of the services of these individuals, or the inability to hire additional key individuals as required, could have a material adverse effect on us, including our current and future product development efforts.</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt; line-height: 1;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-style: italic; font-weight: bold;">Anti-Takeover provisions in Minnesota law may make a hostile takeover of our business more difficult.</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">We are governed by the provisions of Sections <font class=" FactMarked">302</font>A.<font class=" FactMarked">671</font> and <font class=" FactMarked">302</font>A.<font class=" FactMarked">673</font> of the Minnesota Business Corporation Act. These anti-takeover provisions could potentially operate to deny shareholders the receipt of a premium on their common stock and may also have a depressive effect on the market price of our common stock. Section <font class=" FactMarked">302</font>A.<font class=" FactMarked">671</font> generally provides that the shares of a corporation acquired in a &#8220;control share acquisition&#8221; have no voting rights unless voting rights are approved by the shareholders in a prescribed manner. A &#8220;control share acquisition&#8221; is generally defined as an acquisition of beneficial ownership of shares that would, when added to all other shares beneficially owned by the acquiring person, entitle the acquiring person to have voting power of <font class=" FactMarked">20</font>% or more in the election of directors. Section <font class=" FactMarked">302</font>A.<font class=" FactMarked">673</font> prohibits a public corporation from engaging in a &#8220;business combination&#8221; with an &#8220;interested shareholder&#8221; for a period of <font class=" FactMarked">four</font> years after the date of the transaction in which the person became an interested shareholder, unless the business combination is approved in a prescribed manner. A &#8220;business combination&#8221; includes mergers, asset sales and other transactions. An &#8220;interested shareholder&#8221; is a person who is the beneficial owner of <font class=" FactMarked">10</font>% or more of the corporation&#8217;s voting stock. Reference is made to the detailed terms of Sections <font class=" FactMarked">302</font>A.<font class=" FactMarked">671</font> and <font class=" FactMarked">302</font>A.<font class=" FactMarked">673</font> of the Minnesota Business Corporation Act. We have also entered into agreements with certain executive officers that provide for certain benefits upon a change of control. These agreements would make any sale of the Company more expensive to a third party.</font></p>

<p style="margin: 0pt;"><font style="text-decoration: underline;"><font style="color: #000000;"><a style="text-decoration: none; color: #000000; cursor: default; outline: none;" href="#" name="6_S1JPH7YB2O8WGKWG0K884K40S0CGSO" class="customBookmark"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 12pt; font-weight: bold;">Item <font class=" FactMarked">3</font>. Legal Proceedings.</font></a></font></font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">The Company is subject to claims and lawsuits that have been filed in the ordinary course of business. From time to time, the Company brings suit against others to enforce patent rights or to collect debts in the ordinary course of business. The Company is not subject to any pending litigation except as set forth below.</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-weight: bold;">MGC Diagnostics Corporation v. Mr. Guy Martinot and Dr. Jean-Beno&#238;t Martinot</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">In November 2015, the Company commenced litigation in the French-speaking co</font><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">urts of Brussels, Belgium against the selling shareholders of Medisoft for violations of representations and warranties in the stock purchase agreement dated as of July 10, 2014 under which the Company purchased Medisoft. The Company alleged that these violations resulted in Company damages of approximately &#8364;<font class=" FactMarked">985,400</font> ($<font class=" FactMarked">1,084,000</font>).&nbsp;In May 2015, the Company received payment of &#8364;<font class=" FactMarked">406,700</font> ($<font class=" FactMarked">447,000</font>) with respect to these alleged violations pursuant to a bank-guaranteed contractual escrow fund and has reflected that payment on its books and records.&nbsp; <font style="font-size: 10.0pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman','serif'; mso-fareast-font-family: 'Times New Roman'; mso-ansi-language: EN-US; mso-fareast-language: EN-US; mso-bidi-language: AR-SA;">On May 30, 2016, the defendant selling shareholders filed an answer to dispute all claims and asserted a counterclaim against the Company seeking to recover the &#8364;406,700 that was paid to the Company in May 2015 and legal costs. The Company continues to believe the Medisoft selling shareholders are liable to it for violations of representations and warranties in the stock purchase agreement and intends to continue to pursue this matter. The Company has not accrued any losses related to the litigation or accrued any related legal costs it has not yet incurred. The Company currently expects that this litigation process may continue until the fall of 2017.</font> </font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</font>&nbsp;</p>
<p style="margin: 0pt;"><font style="text-decoration: underline;"><font style="color: #000000;"><a style="text-decoration: none; color: #000000; cursor: default; outline: none;" href="#" name="7_WQY96VQM74K8S8SG0K8W8K0SO80CWS" class="customBookmark"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 12pt; font-weight: bold;">Item <font class=" FactMarked">4</font>. Mine Safety Disclosures.</font></a></font></font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">Not applicable.</font></p>

<p style="margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">As of January 20, 2017, there<font style="background-color: #ffffff;"> were <font class=" FactMarked">290</font>&nbsp;shareholders of record who held <font class=" FactMarked">161,000</font> shares of the Company&#8217;s common stock. In addition, nominees held an additional <font class=" FactMarked">4,227,000</font> shares for approximately <font class=" FactMarked">1,000</font> shareholders holding shares in street name.</font></font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; background-color: #ffffff;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-weight: bold;">Dividends</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-weight: bold;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">On March 27, 2013, the Company declared a special cash dividend of&nbsp;$<font class=" FactMarked">0.45</font> per share on its outstanding common stock. The dividend was paid on April 26, 2013 to holders of record as of&nbsp;April 12, 2013.</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;"><br></p>

<p style="margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">The Company&#8217;s Board of Directors will continue to periodically assess the Company&#8217;s capital resources. If the Board determines that the Company&#8217;s capital resources exceed the amount necessary to meet its working capital and liquidity needs, as well as to retain a reasonable cushion for contingencies and strategic opportunities, then the Company will consider various options for increasing shareholder value, including, but not limited to, purchasing its own shares in the open market and in privately negotiated transactions, and paying cash dividends.</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-weight: bold;">Equity Compensation Plan Information</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-weight: bold;">&nbsp;</font>&nbsp;</p>
<p style="margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">At a Special Meeting of Shareholders held on August 22, 2007, the shareholders approved the MGC Diagnostics Corporation <font class=" FactMarked">2007</font> Stock Incentive Plan (the &#8220;<font class=" FactMarked">2007</font> Plan&#8221;) and reserved <font class=" FactMarked">250,000</font> shares of its common stock for issuance under the <font class=" FactMarked">2007</font> Plan. The <font class=" FactMarked">2007</font> Plan has been amended several times and currently authorizes the issuance of up to <font class=" FactMarked">1,150,000</font> shares. As of October 31, 2016, stock options for <font class=" FactMarked">371,733</font>&nbsp;shares were outstanding; <font class=" FactMarked">81,157</font> shares had been issued upon exercise of options; <font class=" FactMarked">404,857</font>&nbsp;shares had been issued pursuant to fully vested restricted stock awards; <font class=" FactMarked">41,497</font>&nbsp;shares were subject to unvested restricted stock awards; <font class=" FactMarked">10,221</font> shares had been issued as performance share awards; <font class=" FactMarked">19,906</font>&nbsp;shares were issued in lieu of quarterly director cash retainer fees and <font class=" FactMarked">220,629</font>&nbsp;shares were available for future grant in some form. Under the terms of the <font class=" FactMarked">2007</font> Plan, as amended, up to <font class=" FactMarked">1,150,000</font> shares may be issued pursuant to incentive stock awards, up to 650,000 may be issued as incentives for non-employee directors and up to 650,000 may be issued pursuant to restricted stock grants. Accordingly, as of October 31, 2016, we could grant <font class=" FactMarked">203,646</font>&nbsp;additional restricted stock awards out of the <font class=" FactMarked">220,629</font>&nbsp;remaining shares authorized under the <font class=" FactMarked">2007</font> Plan.</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;"><br></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">The Company has also adopted the 2006 Employee Stock Purchase Plan. &nbsp;See Note 10 to the consolidated financial statements, "Shareholders' Equity - Employee Stock Purchase Plan."</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">The Company offers&nbsp;a program that allows non-employee Board members to elect and receive shares from the <font class=" FactMarked">2007</font> Plan in lieu of some or all of their quarterly cash retainer fees. During the years ended October 31, 2016 and <font class=" FactMarked">2015</font>, the Company issued <font class=" FactMarked">7,099</font>&nbsp;and <font class=" FactMarked">7,057</font>&nbsp;shares, respectively under this program.</font></p>

<p style="margin: 0pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-weight: bold;">Purchases of Equity Securities By the Issuer and Affiliated Purchasers.</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-weight: bold;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">The Company&#8217;s Board of Directors will continue to periodically assess the Company&#8217;s capital resources. If the Board of Directors determines that the Company&#8217;s capital resources exceed the amount necessary to meet its working capital and liquidity needs, as well as to retain a reasonable cushion for contingencies and strategic opportunities, then the Company will consider various options for increasing shareholder value, including, but not limited to, purchasing its own shares in the open market and in privately negotiated transactions and paying cash dividends.</font></p>

<p align="justify" style="margin: 0px; clear: left; font-family: 'times new roman'; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</p>
<p style="margin: 0pt;"><font style="text-decoration: underline; color: #000000;"><font style="text-decoration: underline;"><a style="text-decoration: none; color: #000000; cursor: default; outline: none; pointer-events: none;" href="#" name="11_649APBXIJKG4OWSW8COG4W0G4WKCO0" class="customBookmark"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 13pt; font-weight: bold;">Item <font class=" FactMarked">7</font>. Management&#8217;s Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations. </font></a></font></font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</font><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-weight: bold;">Overview</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">The Company is a medical device manufacturer with revenues of $<font class=" FactMarked">40.0</font>&nbsp;million for the year ended October 31, 2016. Domestic product sales and service revenue accounted for <font class=" FactMarked">76.5</font>% of fiscal <font class=" FactMarked">2016</font>&nbsp;revenue while international product sales accounted for the remaining <font class=" FactMarked">23.5</font>%. On August 1, 2014, the Company acquired Medisoft SA and subsidiaries to support growth in product offerings and growth within international markets.</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">The Company designs and markets non-invasive cardiorespiratory diagnostic products through its Medical Graphics Corporation and Medisoft SA subsidiaries under the MGC Diagnostics and Medisoft brand and trade names. These products provide solutions for disease detection, integrated care and wellness across the spectrum of cardiorespiratory healthcare. Revenue consists of equipment, supplies and accessory sales as well as service sales. Equipment, supplies and accessory sales reflect sales of non-invasive cardiorespiratory diagnostic equipment, interface, test and communication software and accessories, as well as, aftermarket sales of peripherals, supplies and software. Service revenue consists of revenue from extended service contracts and non-warranty service.</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-weight: bold;">Seasonality</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-weight: bold;">&nbsp;</font><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-weight: bold;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">The Company experiences some seasonality in its revenues, with the fourth quarter of its fiscal year traditionally being its strongest quarter. The Company experiences variability in quarterly results <font class=" FactMarked">due</font> to a number of factors, including customer budget cycles, product introductions, Company sales incentive programs, the Company&#8217;s ability to convert competitor accounts, general economic conditions and the timing of customer orders.</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">Although the Company currently expects fiscal <font class=" FactMarked">2017</font>&nbsp;revenues to increase over fiscal <font class=" FactMarked">2016</font>&nbsp;revenues, the Company expects quarter-over-quarter results to vary during the fiscal year, <font class=" FactMarked">due</font> to seasonality and other factors listed above.</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-weight: bold;">Recent K</font><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-weight: bold;">ey Developments:</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-weight: bold;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<div class=" ParaMarked">
<table cellspacing="0" cellpadding="0" style="border-collapse: collapse; margin-left: 0pt; width: 100%;" width="100%">

<tr>
<td style="vertical-align: top; width: 18pt;">
<p><font style="font-family: Symbol; font-size: 10pt; background-color: #ffffff;"> &#61623; </font></p>
</td>
<td style="vertical-align: top;">
<p style="margin: 0pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; background-color: #ffffff;">Fiscal 2016 operating loss&nbsp;was $(2.6&nbsp;million) compared to operating income&nbsp;of $<font class=" FactMarked">1.6</font>&nbsp;million in fiscal <font class=" FactMarked">2015</font>. The fiscal 2016 operating loss included charges of $3,313,000 for Medisoft goodwill impairment, $298,000 for impairment of certain&nbsp;Medisoft intangible assets, and $670,000 and $354,000 for inventory reserves related to Resmon PRO FOT and SleepVirtual diagnostic inventory, respectively, as well as $650,000 of costs for a legal settlement with the manufacturer of the SleepVirtual inventory. Fiscal <font class=" FactMarked">2016</font> net loss&nbsp;was $(3.8&nbsp;million) or $(<font class=" FactMarked">0.88)</font>&nbsp;per diluted share, compared to fiscal 2015 net income of $4.0 million or $0.94 per diluted share, including (i) the recognition of a $3.1&nbsp;million domestic tax benefit related to the partial reversal of the valuation allowance on deferred tax assets related to Medical Graphics&#8217; net operating loss carryforwards and (ii) $0.54&nbsp;million deferred tax benefit in foreign operations. </font></p>
</td>
</tr>

<td style="vertical-align: top;">
<p style="margin: 0pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; background-color: #ffffff;"> Our continued focus on selling extended service agreements at the time of initial system purchase continues to sustain our service revenues. Domestic service revenues were $7.0 million for fiscal 2016 compared to $6.8 million for fiscal 2015. The Attachment Rate, which reflects the percentage of Extended Service Contracts added at the point of sale to customer equipment purchases, was 31.2% and 31.5% for fiscal <font class=" FactMarked">2016</font> and <font class=" FactMarked">2015</font>, respectively. The Company had combined current and long-term deferred revenue of $7.6 million and $6.2 million as of October 31, 2016 and 2015, respectively, associated with service contract agreements.</font></p>

<td style="vertical-align: top;">
<p style="margin: 0pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; background-color: #ffffff;"> In line with our strategic objective to grow revenues faster than the market growth, we have focused on converting competitor accounts into MGC Diagnostics customers. Fiscal <font class=" FactMarked">2016</font> domestic equipment and accessories revenues included 89&nbsp;competitive conversions ($<font class=" FactMarked">5.6</font> million in revenue), compared to <font class=" FactMarked">66</font>&nbsp;competitive conversions ($<font class=" FactMarked">3.1</font>&nbsp;million in revenue) during fiscal <font class=" FactMarked">2015</font>. Excluding the effect of revenue from competitive conversions in each period, Medical Graphics domestic equipment and accessories revenue generated from existing customers grew 6.3% in fiscal <font class=" FactMarked">2016</font>, compared to fiscal <font class=" FactMarked">2015</font>. </font></p>
</td>
</tr>

<p style="margin: 0pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;"><font style="font-family: 'times new roman', times; font-size: 10pt;">The following paragraphs discuss the Company&#8217;s performance for fiscal years ended October 31, 2016 and <font class=" FactMarked">2015</font>.</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;"><font style="font-family: 'times new roman', times; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;"><font style="font-family: 'times new roman', times; font-size: 10pt;">The Company operates in a single industry segment, the manufacture and sale of cardiorespiratory diagnostic products. The following discussion segregates information with respect to Medical Graphics and Medisoft. Combined results for Medical Graphics and Medisoft are referred to as &#8220;Consolidated&#8221; results.</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;"><font style="font-family: 'times new roman', times; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-weight: bold;">Revenues</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">Fiscal <font class=" FactMarked">2016</font> consolidated revenues increased <font class=" FactMarked">6.9</font>% to $<font class=" FactMarked">40.0</font> million, compared to $<font class=" FactMarked">37.5</font> million for fiscal <font class=" FactMarked">2015</font>. Medical Graphics&#8217; fiscal <font class=" FactMarked">2016</font> total revenue increased 7.3% to $<font class=" FactMarked">34.4</font>&nbsp;million, compared to $<font class=" FactMarked">32.0</font>&nbsp;million for fiscal <font class=" FactMarked">2015</font>. Medisoft&#8217;s fiscal <font class=" FactMarked">2016</font> total revenue was $<font class=" FactMarked">5.7</font>&nbsp;million, compared to $<font class=" FactMarked">5.4</font> million for fiscal <font class=" FactMarked">2015</font>, a <font class=" FactMarked">4.3</font>% increase.</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">Fiscal <font class=" FactMarked">2016</font> domestic equipment and accessories revenues for Medical Graphics included <font class=" FactMarked">89</font> competitive conversions ($<font class=" FactMarked">5.6</font> million in revenue), compared to <font class=" FactMarked">66</font> competitive conversions ($<font class=" FactMarked">3.1</font>&nbsp;million in revenue) for fiscal <font class=" FactMarked">2015</font>. Excluding the effect of revenue from competitive conversions in each period, Medical Graphics domestic equipment and accessories revenue generated from existing customers grew <font class=" FactMarked">6.3</font>% in fiscal <font class=" FactMarked">2016</font>&nbsp;compared to fiscal <font class=" FactMarked">2015</font>.</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">Domestic service revenues, all of which were contributed by Medical Graphics, increased <font class=" FactMarked">2.1</font>% to $<font class=" FactMarked">7.0</font> million, compared to $<font class=" FactMarked">6.8</font> million for fiscal <font class=" FactMarked">2015</font>. The Attachment Rate, which reflects the percentage of Extended Service Contracts added at the point of sale to customer equipment purchases, was <font class=" FactMarked">31.2</font>% for fiscal <font class=" FactMarked">2016</font> and 31.5% for fiscal&nbsp;<font class=" FactMarked">2015</font>.</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;"><font style="font-family: 'times new roman', times; font-size: 10pt;">Consolidated international equipment, supplies and accessories revenues&nbsp;decreased&nbsp;<font class=" FactMarked">10.8</font>% to $<font class=" FactMarked">9.4</font>&nbsp;million, compared to $<font class=" FactMarked">10.6</font>&nbsp;million for fiscal <font class=" FactMarked">2015</font>, <font class=" FactMarked">due</font> primarily to a 22.7% reduction in international equipment sales from Medical Graphics.</font></p>
<p align="justify" style="margin: 0px; clear: left; font-family: 'times new roman'; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</p>
<p style="margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">Medical Graphics domestic recurring revenue, consisting of supplies and services revenues, grew to $<font class=" FactMarked">13.8</font> million representing&nbsp;<font class=" FactMarked">34.4</font>% of consolidated fiscal <font class=" FactMarked">2016</font> revenues compared to <font class=" FactMarked">35.2</font>% of fiscal <font class=" FactMarked">2015</font> revenues.</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">Sales backlog at the end of fiscal <font class=" FactMarked">2016</font> was $<font class=" FactMarked">1.5</font> million ($<font class=" FactMarked">1.2</font> million for Medical Graphics and $<font class=" FactMarked">0.3</font>&nbsp;million for Medisoft), compared to $<font class=" FactMarked">2.6</font> million at the end of fiscal <font class=" FactMarked">2015</font>, which was an all-time high.</font></p>

<p style="margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">The Company anticipates revenue growth in the near term <font class=" FactMarked">due</font> to its current sales backlog and its pipeline of new sales opportunities. Sustained seasonal growth for all of fiscal <font class=" FactMarked">2017</font>&nbsp;will depend on the rate at which current customers replace older devices and the Company&#8217;s ability to continue taking business&nbsp;away from its competition.&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-weight: bold;">Gross Margin</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">Gross margin for fiscal <font class=" FactMarked">2016</font> was <font class=" FactMarked">50.4</font>% (<font class=" FactMarked">52.2</font>% for Medical Graphics and <font class=" FactMarked">39.6</font>% for Medisoft), compared to <font class=" FactMarked">51.6</font>% for fiscal <font class=" FactMarked">2015</font> (<font class=" FactMarked">54.1</font>% for Medical Graphics and <font class=" FactMarked">36.7</font>% for Medisoft). Gross margin for equipment, supplies and accessories was <font class=" FactMarked">46.2</font>% (<font class=" FactMarked">47.6</font>% for Medical Graphics and <font class=" FactMarked">39.6</font>% for Medisoft), compared to <font class=" FactMarked">47.5</font>% for fiscal <font class=" FactMarked">2015</font> (<font class=" FactMarked">49.8</font>% for Medical Graphics and <font class=" FactMarked">36.7</font>% for Medisoft). Gross margin for fiscal 2016 for services was <font class=" FactMarked">70.2</font>%, compared to <font class=" FactMarked">69.8</font>% for fiscal <font class=" FactMarked">2015</font>. </font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;"><br></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">Fiscal 2016 gross margin was adversely affected by charges of $354,000 and $670,000 for inventory valuation reserves for&nbsp;the Company's SleepVirtual and Resmon PRO FOT inventory, respectively (3.0% of Medical Graphics revenue; 2.6% of consolidated revenues). These reserves&nbsp;were recorded as a result of the fiscal fourth quarter review and assessment, which indicated that these inventories exceeded&nbsp;the forecasted unit sales determined in the development of the Fiscal 2017 operating budget.&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">The Company expects to maintain total gross margin in the mid-<font class=" FactMarked">50</font>% range for Medical Graphics during fiscal <font class=" FactMarked">2017</font>, absent significant change in volume and product mix or additional inventory impairment. Although Medisoft gross margin has improved during fiscal <font class=" FactMarked">2016</font>&nbsp;compared to fiscal <font class=" FactMarked">2015</font>, continued improvement of Medisoft gross margin will depend on its ability to increase&nbsp;its revenue to better leverage its fixed costs of production.</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-weight: bold;">Selling and Marketing</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">Selling and marketing expenses for fiscal <font class=" FactMarked">2016</font> increased by <font class=" FactMarked">19.1</font>%, or $<font class=" FactMarked">1.7</font>&nbsp;million, to $<font class=" FactMarked">10.5</font> million compared to $<font class=" FactMarked">8.8</font> million for fiscal <font class=" FactMarked">2015</font>. This expense increase was comprised of increases of $1,280,000 and $404,000 for Medical Graphics and Medisoft, respectively, compared to fiscal <font class=" FactMarked">2015</font>. For Medical Graphics fiscal <font class=" FactMarked">2016</font> expenses compared to <font class=" FactMarked">2015</font>, there was a $<font class=" FactMarked">619,000</font> increase in sales commissions and buying group fees, a $<font class=" FactMarked">316,000</font>&nbsp;increase in telemarketing services, a $<font class=" FactMarked">183,000</font> increase in consulting fees, a $<font class=" FactMarked">143,000</font>&nbsp;increase in personnel costs and a $<font class=" FactMarked">97,000</font>&nbsp;increase&nbsp;in promotion and demonstration expenses, offset in part by a decrease of $119,000 in management incentives. Medisoft increases relate primarily to realignment of personnel resources for fiscal 2016 compared to 2015.</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-weight: bold;">General and Administrative</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">General and administrative expenses for <font class=" FactMarked">2016</font> were flat at&nbsp;$<font class=" FactMarked">5.7</font> million compared to <font class=" FactMarked">2015</font>. Fiscal <font class=" FactMarked">2016</font>&nbsp;Medical Graphics expenses increased&nbsp;by $<font class=" FactMarked">650,000</font>&nbsp;due to a legal settlement with Neurovirtual USA, Inc. with respect to a termination of an inventory distribution agreement, a $<font class=" FactMarked">205,000</font>&nbsp;increase in net personnel and consulting costs and a&nbsp;$92,000 increase in legal expenses, which were partially offset by a $435,000 decrease in Medisoft integration expenses compared to the&nbsp;prior year and a $151,000 decrease in management incentives.</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-weight: bold;">Research and Development</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">Research and development expenses for <font class=" FactMarked">2016</font>&nbsp;decreased by <font class=" FactMarked">8.6</font>%, or $<font class=" FactMarked">0.2</font>&nbsp;million, to $<font class=" FactMarked">2.7</font> million compared to $<font class=" FactMarked">2.9</font> million in <font class=" FactMarked">2015</font>. This decrease is primarily in Medical Graphics expenses&nbsp;<font class=" FactMarked">due</font> to $<font class=" FactMarked">141,000</font>&nbsp;of personnel and consultant costs, an $<font class=" FactMarked">80,000</font> net decrease in project-related material costs&nbsp;and $<font class=" FactMarked">68,000</font> of management incentives. The hardware and software development expense reductions&nbsp;of $358,000 in 2016 were offset in part by $162,000 of increases in hardware and software sustaining costs, compared to fiscal 2015 expenses. The Company capitalized software development costs of $<font class=" FactMarked">739,000</font> in <font class=" FactMarked">2016</font> and $<font class=" FactMarked">740,000</font> in <font class=" FactMarked">2015</font>.</font></p>
<p align="justify" style="margin: 0px; clear: left; font-family: 'times new roman'; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</p>
<p style="margin: 0pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-weight: bold;">Impairment of Goodwill</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt;"><br></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;"> <font style="font-size: 10.0pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman','serif'; mso-fareast-font-family: 'Times New Roman'; mso-ansi-language: EN-US; mso-fareast-language: EN-US; mso-bidi-language: AR-SA;">During the&nbsp;fiscal 2016 fourth quarter, management met with our Board of Directors to present, discuss and obtain approval of the fiscal 2017 budget for Medical Graphics and Medisoft.&nbsp; During this meeting, Medisoft&#8217;s fiscal 2017 revenue, gross margin and operating expense metrics were forecast to be comparable to fiscal 2016 actual results. The fiscal 2017 Medisoft budget that was approved by the Board forecast less favorable results than the preliminary budget the Company had forecast when it reviewed potential triggering events during the fiscal 2016 third quarter. Using the less favorable fiscal 2017 Medisoft budget as the baseline, management developed a long-range financial projection that it used to determine an enterprise fair value for Medisoft. The outcome of this long-range projection showed lower revenue and profitability for future years than what the Company had forecast in the past. The lower long-range projection resulted in an implied enterprise fair value for Medisoft that was significantly below its book carrying value, resulting in the full impairment of goodwill. As a result, the Company recorded a charge of $3,313,000 for the impairment of the full balance of the goodwill from the Medisoft acquisition.</font></font></p>

<p style="margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-weight: bold;">Amortization of Intangibles</font></p>
<p align="justify" style="margin: 0px; clear: left; font-family: 'times new roman'; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</p>
<p style="margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">Amortization costs increased by $0.3&nbsp;million to $.5&nbsp;million for the year ended October 31, 2016 compared to $<font class=" FactMarked">0.2</font>&nbsp;million for the year ended October 31, 2015. In connection with the testing of long-lived assets in the fourth fiscal quarter, the Company also determined that the unamortized original value of $298,000 assigned to two patents and in-process research and development were deemed to be impaired because the asset was either abandoned or future revenue and cash flow streams could not be forecasted for these assets.</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">In addition, in fiscal <font class=" FactMarked">2016</font>, the Company's cost of equipment revenues included approximately $<font class=" FactMarked">336,000</font> of amortization related to capitalized software development costs compared to $<font class=" FactMarked">379,000</font> in fiscal <font class=" FactMarked">2015</font>. The fiscal <font class=" FactMarked">2016</font> amortization included $<font class=" FactMarked">245,000</font>&nbsp;and the fiscal 2015 amortization included $266,000 of recorded impairment for software that&nbsp;was deemed to have no future value.</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-weight: bold;">Interest Expense</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">Interest expense for <font class=" FactMarked">2016</font>, net of interest income, was $<font class=" FactMarked">188,000</font> compared to $<font style="color: #000000; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 13.3333px; font-style: normal; font-variant-ligatures: normal; font-variant-caps: normal; font-weight: normal; letter-spacing: normal; orphans: 2; text-align: start; text-indent: 48px; text-transform: none; white-space: normal; widows: 2; word-spacing: 0px; -webkit-text-stroke-width: 0px; background-color: #ffffff; display: inline !important; float: none;"><font class=" FactMarked">247</font></font>,<font class=" FactMarked">000</font> in <font class=" FactMarked">2015</font>. The decrease in interest expense is related to the fiscal 2016 payoff of the remainder of the $<font class=" FactMarked">4.0</font> million term loan the Company used to partially finance the acquisition of Medisoft on August 1, 2014. Interest rates were variable in relation to the lender&#8217;s base rate. The Company earns interest income on excess cash, which is consistent with the Company&#8217;s goal of preserving capital. In fiscal <font class=" FactMarked">2015</font>, interest income included interest of $<font class=" FactMarked">29,000</font> related to the Company&#8217;s receipt of a research and development credit from the State of Minnesota.</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-weight: bold;">Provision for Taxes</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; background-color: #ffffff;"> <font style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', serif; background-image: initial; background-position: initial; background-size: initial; background-repeat: initial; background-attachment: initial; background-origin: initial; background-clip: initial;">In the quarter ended October 31, 2016, the Company early adopted ASU 2016-09, <i style="mso-bidi-font-style: normal;">Improvements to Employee Share-Based Payment Accounting</i>.<font style="mso-spacerun: yes;">&nbsp; </font>The standard simplifies various aspects of the accounting and presentation of share-based payments including the income tax consequences.<font style="mso-spacerun: yes;">&nbsp; </font>The impact of the adoption of this standard is more fully described in Note 12.</font></font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;">&nbsp;<br></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; background-color: #ffffff;">The Company recorded a net income tax expense&nbsp;of $<font class=" FactMarked">923,000</font> in fiscal <font class=" FactMarked">2016</font> compared to a $<font style="color: #000000; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 13.3333px; font-style: normal; font-variant-ligatures: normal; font-variant-caps: normal; font-weight: normal; letter-spacing: normal; orphans: 2; text-align: start; text-indent: 48px; text-transform: none; white-space: normal; widows: 2; word-spacing: 0px; -webkit-text-stroke-width: 0px; float: none; display: inline !important;"><font class=" FactMarked">3,549</font></font>,<font class=" FactMarked">000</font> income tax benefit in fiscal <font class=" FactMarked">2015</font>. The fiscal 2016&nbsp;income tax <font style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', serif; background-image: initial; background-position: initial; background-size: initial; background-repeat: initial; background-attachment: initial; background-origin: initial; background-clip: initial;">expense includes U.S deferred expense of approximately $</font><font style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', serif; background-image: initial; background-position: initial; background-size: initial; background-repeat: initial; background-attachment: initial; background-origin: initial; background-clip: initial;">593,000</font><font style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', serif; background-image: initial; background-position: initial; background-size: initial; background-repeat: initial; background-attachment: initial; background-origin: initial; background-clip: initial;">, and foreign deferred expense of approximately $</font><font style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', serif; background-image: initial; background-position: initial; background-size: initial; background-repeat: initial; background-attachment: initial; background-origin: initial; background-clip: initial;">106,000&nbsp;</font><font style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', serif; background-image: initial; background-position: initial; background-size: initial; background-repeat: initial; background-attachment: initial; background-origin: initial; background-clip: initial;">related to Medisoft Belgium.<font style="mso-spacerun: yes;">&nbsp;</font>The U.S. current tax includes state taxes, minimum fees and federal AMT of approximately </font><font style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', serif; background-image: initial; background-position: initial; background-size: initial; background-repeat: initial; background-attachment: initial; background-origin: initial; background-clip: initial;">$206,000</font><font style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', serif; background-image: initial; background-position: initial; background-size: initial; background-repeat: initial; background-attachment: initial; background-origin: initial; background-clip: initial;">, and an increase in reserve for uncertain tax positions totaling $18,000</font><font style="font-size: 10.0pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman','serif'; mso-fareast-font-family: 'Times New Roman'; mso-ansi-language: EN-US; mso-fareast-language: EN-US; mso-bidi-language: AR-SA;">.</font></font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; background-color: #ffffff;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; background-color: #ffffff;">The Company will continue to assess the potential realization of its remaining deferred tax assets in the future to determine if sufficient evidence exists to remove all or a portion of the Company&#8217;s&nbsp;remaining valuation allowance on its deferred tax assets. In making this assessment, management considers the scheduled reversal of deferred tax liabilities, projected future taxable income and tax planning strategies. The Company has not yet achieved the more-likely-than-not threshold for the remaining valuation allowance of (i) approximately $<font class=" FactMarked">1,952,000</font> in place on its domestic deferred tax assets and (ii) approximately $772<font class=" FactMarked">,000</font> related to its Belgium, Italy, Germany, France and Belgium S.P.R.L. subsidiaries deferred tax assets. Any reversal of the remaining valuation allowance on the Company&#8217;s deferred tax assets may have a substantial impact on profitability in the period of the reversal. For additional information see Note <font class=" FactMarked">12</font> to the consolidated financial statements, &#8220;Income Taxes.&#8221;</font></p>
<p align="justify" style="margin: 0px; clear: left; font-family: 'times new roman'; font-size: 10pt;"><font style="background-color: #ffffff;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-weight: bold;">Liquidity and Capital Resources</font></p>
<p align="justify" style="margin: 0px; clear: left; font-family: 'times new roman'; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</p>
<p style="margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">The Company had cash of $<font class=" FactMarked">7.3</font> million and working capital of $<font class=" FactMarked">11.7</font> million as of October 31, 2016. During <font class=" FactMarked">2016</font>, the Company generated $<font class=" FactMarked">4.6</font> million in cash from operating activities, with $<font class=" FactMarked">3.3</font>&nbsp;million generated before changes in working capital items. Net increases in <font class=" FactMarked">2016</font> cash from working capital of $<font class=" FactMarked">1,249,000</font>&nbsp;consisted principally of a $<font class=" FactMarked">1,554,000</font> increase in deferred income collected, $<font class=" FactMarked">850,000</font>&nbsp;decrease in inventory, $<font class=" FactMarked">269,000</font>&nbsp;decrease in prepaid and other current assets, a $<font class=" FactMarked">244,000</font>&nbsp;increase in accounts payable, offset by an $<font class=" FactMarked">848,000</font> increase in accounts receivable, an $518,000 decrease in other current liabilities and accrued expenses, and a $<font class=" FactMarked">302,000</font>&nbsp;decrease in employee compensation accruals. Days sales outstanding (&#8220;DSO&#8221;), which measures how quickly receivables are collected, increased by <font class=" FactMarked">1</font> day to <font class=" FactMarked">65</font>&nbsp;days from <font class=" FactMarked">2015</font>&nbsp;to <font class=" FactMarked">2016</font>, which decreased cash flows. Inventory decreased by $<font class=" FactMarked">1,843,000</font>&nbsp;($993,000 from non-cash impairment reserves), as days of inventory on hand decreased by <font class=" FactMarked">51</font> days to <font class=" FactMarked">70</font>&nbsp;days in <font class=" FactMarked">2016</font>. The accounts payable balance increased by $<font class=" FactMarked">244,000</font>, increasing cash flow and decreasing days payables outstanding by <font class=" FactMarked">9</font>&nbsp;days to <font class=" FactMarked">38</font>&nbsp;days in <font class=" FactMarked">2016</font>. Employee compensation accruals as of October 31, 2016 were lower compared to October 31, 2015&nbsp;<font class=" FactMarked">due</font> to a decrease for the <font class=" FactMarked">2016</font>&nbsp;management incentive bonus program.</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</font>&nbsp;</p>

<p style="margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">During <font class=" FactMarked">2016</font>, the Company used $<font class=" FactMarked">907,000</font> in cash for the purchase of property, equipment and intangible assets. The Company had no material commitments outstanding for capital expenditures for fiscal year <font class=" FactMarked">2016</font>. The Company is continuing its investment in the initiative to migrate its products&#8217; operating software to a next generation software platform, including expensed development efforts and capitalized software development costs, as it pursues approval of this software platform with the Food and Drug Administration during fiscal 2017. During <font class=" FactMarked">2016</font>, the Company used&nbsp;$<font class=" FactMarked">3.0</font>&nbsp;million to pay off the remaining principal balance on its long-term loan. The Company has no debt or an available line of credit.</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">The Company&#8217;s Board of Directors will continue to periodically assess the Company&#8217;s capital resources. If the Board of Directors determines that the Company&#8217;s capital resources exceed the amount necessary to meet its working capital and liquidity needs, as well as to retain a reasonable cushion for contingencies and strategic opportunities, then the Company will consider various options for increasing shareholder value, including, but not limited to, purchasing its own shares in the open market and in privately negotiated transactions and paying cash dividends.</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</font>&nbsp;&nbsp;</p>
<p style="margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">On January 25, 2017, the Company declared a special cash dividend of $0.70 per share on its outstanding common stock. The dividend will be paid on February 24, 2017 to holders of record as of February 10, 2017. The Company believes that its cash balance after payment of the dividend&nbsp;will be sufficient to fund its&nbsp;operations and working capital requirements and permit anticipated capital expenditures during the upcoming year. We may pursue acquisitions of other companies or product lines, which if successful may require additional funding sources. </font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;"><br></p>
<p align="justify" style="margin: 0px; clear: left; font-family: 'times new roman'; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</p>
<p style="margin: 0pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-weight: bold; background-color: #ffffff;">Critical Accounting Policies</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; background-color: #ffffff;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; background-color: #ffffff;">Significant accounting policies adopted and applied by the Company are summarized in Note <font class=" FactMarked">2</font> to the consolidated financial statements, &#8220;Summary of Significant Accounting Policies,&#8221; which is included in this Form 10-K. Some of the more critical policies include revenue recognition, reserve for inventory obsolescence, allowance for doubtful accounts, internal software development costs, income taxes, stock-based compensation and impairment of long-lived assets, intangible assets and goodwill. Management considers the following accounting policies to be the most critical to the presentation of the consolidated financial statements because they require the most difficult, subjective and complex judgments.</font></p>
<p align="justify" style="margin: 0px; clear: left; font-family: 'times new roman'; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</p>
<p style="margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;"><font style="background-color: #ffffff;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-style: italic; font-weight: bold;">Revenue Recognition. </font><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">The Company recognizes revenue when persuasive evidence of an arrangement exists, transfer of title has occurred or services have been rendered, the selling price is fixed or determinable and collectability is reasonably assured. The Company&#8217;s products are sold for cash or on credit terms requiring payment based on the shipment date. Credit terms can vary between customers <font class=" FactMarked">due</font> to many factors, but are generally <font class=" FactMarked">30</font> to <font class=" FactMarked">60</font> days. Revenue, net of discounts, is generally recognized upon shipment or delivery to customers in accordance with written sales terms. Standard sales terms do not include customer acceptance conditions, future credits, rebates or general rights of return. The terms of sales to both domestic customers and international distributors are similar though in some instances longer for international customers. In instances when a customer order specifies final acceptance of the system, the Company defers recognition of revenue until all customer acceptance criteria have been met. In certain situations customer requested short-term bill-and-hold arrangements have been accommodated and accounted for in accordance with authoritative literature. Estimated warranty obligations are recorded upon shipment<font style="background-color: #ffffff;">. Sales and use taxes are reported on a net basis, excluding them from revenues and cost of revenues.</font></font></font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; background-color: #ffffff;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<div class="pageBreak">
<div class=" ParaMarked">

</div>
