<p style="margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;"><br></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-weight: bold;">Inventory Measurement</font><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;"> &#8211; In July 2015, FASB issued ASU 2015-11, <em>Inventory</em></font><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-style: italic;">&nbsp;(Topic 330)</font><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;&nbsp;</font><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-style: italic;">Simplifying the Measurement of Inventory</font><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;"> which applies to all inventory except inventory that is measured using last-in, first-out (LIFO) or the retail inventory method. Inventory measured using first-in, first-out (FIFO) or average cost is covered by the new amendments. Inventory within the scope of the new guidance should be measured at the lower of cost and net realizable value. Net realizable value is the estimated selling prices in the ordinary course of business, less reasonably predictable costs of completion, disposal, and transportation. Subsequent measurement is unchanged for inventory measured using LIFO or the retail inventory method. The amendments will take effect for public business entities for fiscal years beginning after December 15, 2016, including interim periods within those fiscal years. The new guidance should be applied prospectively, and earlier application is permitted as of the beginning of an interim or annual reporting period. The Company is evaluating the impact of the standard on the consolidated financial statements.</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;"><strong>Employee Share-based Payment Accounting</strong>&nbsp;&#8211; In March&nbsp;2016, the FASB issued ASU 2016-09, </font><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-style: italic;">Income Taxes (Topic 718) Improvements to Employee Share-based Compensation Accounting,</font><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;which simplifies various aspects of accounting for share-based payments to employees. Key provisions of the new standard include requiring excess tax benefits and shortfalls to be recorded as income tax benefit or expense in the income statement rather than in equity, and permitting an election to record the impact of pre-vesting forfeitures as they occur. The new guidance is effective fiscal years beginning after December 15, 2016, with early adoption available. The Company elected to early adopt ASU 2016-09 during the quarter ended October 31, 2016, retroactive to November 1, 2015. See Note 12 of the consolidated statements "Income Taxes"&nbsp;for details of the impact to the Company's consolidated financial statements.</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;"><br></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;"><strong>L<font>ease Accounting</font> <font style="color: #000000; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 13.3333px; font-style: normal; font-variant-ligatures: normal; font-variant-caps: normal; font-weight: normal; letter-spacing: normal; orphans: 2; text-align: start; text-indent: 48px; text-transform: none; white-space: normal; widows: 2; word-spacing: 0px; -webkit-text-stroke-width: 0px; background-color: #ffffff; display: inline !important; float: none;">&#8211;</font>&nbsp;</strong>During February 2016, FASB issued ASU No. 2016-02, <em>Leases</em>. ASU No. 2016-02 was issued to increase transparency and comparability among organizations by recognizing all lease transactions (with terms in excess of 12 months) on the balance sheet as a lease liability and a right-of-use asset (as defined). ASU No. 2016-02 is effective for fiscal years beginning after December 15, 2018, including interim periods within those fiscal years, with earlier application permitted. Upon adoption, the lessee will apply the new standard using a modified retrospective transition method. The Company is currently assessing the effect that ASU No. 2016-02 will have on its consolidated financial statements.</font></p>

<td style="vertical-align: top; width: 4%;">
<p style="margin: 0pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-weight: bold;"> (<font class=" FactMarked">3</font>) </font></p>
</td>
<td style="vertical-align: top; width: 96%;">
<p style="margin: 0pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-weight: bold;">&nbsp; &nbsp;Medisoft Acquisition Matters</font></p>
</td>
</tr>

</table>
</div>
<p style="margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">On August 1, 2014, MGC Diagnostics Corporation acquired <font class="TaggedFact">100</font>% of the stock of Medisoft SA (&#8220;Medisoft&#8221;), through its newly established wholly-owned subsidiary, MGC Diagnostics Belgium S.P.R.L., a private limited liability company. Medisoft, based in Sorinnes, Belgium, was a privately held manufacturer of cardiorespiratory diagnostics</font><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;"> products, with operating subsidiaries in France, Germany and Italy. The Company is using&nbsp;the acquisition to expand its product range and provide a platform for global expansion outside the United States.</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">The Company acquired Medisoft for total cash consideration of &#8364;<font class="TaggedFact">5,780,000</font> ($<font class="TaggedFact">7,745,000</font>). In addition, at closing, MGC Diagnostics issued to the Medisoft selling shareholders warrants to purchase <font class="TaggedFact">168,342</font> shares of MGC Diagnostics common stock at a price of $<font class="TaggedFact">7.96</font> per share. The warrants have a <font class="TaggedFact">three</font>-year term expiring on August 1, 2017. The value of the warrants was approximately &#8364;<font class="TaggedFact">314,000</font> ($<font class="TaggedFact">421,000</font>). The warrants were valued at $<font class="TaggedFact">2.50</font> per share using the Black-Scholes model assuming an expected life of <font class="TaggedFact">three</font> years; risk free interest rate of <font class="TaggedFact">1.0</font>%; volatility of</font><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;"> <font class="TaggedFact">45.0</font>% and dividend yield of <font class="TaggedFact">0</font>%.</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">Of the total cash consideration, &#8364;<font class="TaggedFact">4,067,000</font> ($<font class="TaggedFact">5,449,000</font>) was paid to the Medisoft former shareholders to purchase the Medisoft stock and &#8364;<font class="TaggedFact">1,713,000</font> ($<font class="TaggedFact">2,296,000</font>) was used to retire existing Medisoft indebtedness.</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;"><br></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">In the quarter ended July 31, 2015, the Company adjusted the initial purchase price allocation as of the August 1, 2014 acquisition date to reflect modifications to the fair value of certain assets and liabilities. &nbsp;These adjustments reflected the addition of unrecorded liabilities that existed at the acquisition date, partially offset by approximately $447,000 in cash from a bank guarantee that was established as part of the July 2014 stock purchase agreement to compensate the Company for potential violations of representations and warranties in the agreement.</font></p>
<div class="ExcludeValue">
<div class="ExcludeValue">
<p align="justify" style="margin: 0px; clear: left; font-family: 'times new roman'; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">The goodwill value that resulted from this acquisition was principally derived from the nature and quality of the products offered that are complementary to the Company&#8217;s current business, Medisoft&#8217;s reputation in the market, synergies that were expected from markets outside the United States when combined with the Company&#8217;s existing foreign operations and the competitive cost structure that the acquired operations offer. The goodwill is not deductible for tax purposes because the Company acquired 100% of the outstanding shares of Medisoft and its wholly-owned subsidiaries. &nbsp;No changes occurred to recorded goodwill other than as described above and the effects of currency translation in the consolidated balance sheet&nbsp;as of October 31, 2015. The Company performed its annual review of the goodwill valuation as of September 30, 2016 given its judgment that there had been no earlier triggering events. <font style="font-size: 10.0pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman','serif'; mso-fareast-font-family: 'Times New Roman'; mso-ansi-language: EN-US; mso-fareast-language: EN-US; mso-bidi-language: AR-SA;">During the fiscal 2016 fourth quarter, management met with our Board of Directors to present, discuss and obtain approval of the fiscal 2017 budget for Medical Graphics and Medisoft. During this meeting, Medisoft&#8217;s fiscal 2017 revenue, gross margin and operating expense metrics were forecast to be comparable to fiscal 2016 actual results. The fiscal 2017 Medisoft budget that was approved by the Board forecast less favorable results than the preliminary budget the Company had forecast when it reviewed potential triggering events during the fiscal 2016 third quarter.&nbsp; Using the less favorable fiscal 2017 Medisoft budget as the baseline, management developed a long-range financial projection that it used to determine an enterprise fair value for Medisoft. The outcome of this long-range projection showed lower revenue and profitability for future years than what the Company had forecast in the past. The lower long-range projection resulted in an implied enterprise fair value for Medisoft that was significantly below its book carrying value, resulting in the full impairment of goodwill. </font>As a result, the Company recorded a charge <font>of $<font><font class="TaggedFact">3,313,000</font></font></font>&nbsp;for the impairment of the full balance of the goodwill from the Medisoft acquisition. &nbsp;Cumulative foreign exchange translation losses with respect to goodwill valuation of $<font class="TaggedFact">11,000</font> and $<font class="TaggedFact">725,000</font> as of October 31, 2016 and 2015, respectively, are included in accumulated other comprehensive loss as reported in the consolidated balance sheet.</font></p>
</div>
<p style="margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</font></p><div class="TaggedFact">

<tr>
<td style="vertical-align: top; width: 36pt;">
<p style="margin: 0pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-weight: bold;">(4)</font></p>

<td style="vertical-align: top;">
<p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-weight: bold;"> Fair Value Measurements </font></p>
</td>
</tr>

</table>
<p style="margin: 0pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="background-color: #ffffff; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">A hierarchy for inputs used in measuring fair value is in place that distinguishes market data between observable independent market inputs and unobservable market assumptions by the reporting entity. The hierarchy is intended to maximize the use of observable inputs and minimize the use of unobservable inputs by requiring that the most observable inputs be used when available. <font class=" FactMarked">Three</font> levels within the hierarchy may be used to measure fair value:</font></p>
<p style="background-color: #ffffff; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<table cellspacing="0" cellpadding="0" style="border-collapse: collapse; margin-left: 0pt; width: 100%;" width="100%">

<tr>
<td style="vertical-align: top; width: 18pt;">
<p style="margin: 0pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;"> &nbsp; </font></p>
</td>
<td style="vertical-align: top; width: 18pt;">
<p style="margin: 0pt;"><font style="font-family: Symbol; font-size: 10pt;"> &#61623; </font></p>
</td>
<td style="vertical-align: top;">
<p style="margin: 0pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;"> Level <font class=" FactMarked">1</font>: Inputs are unadjusted quoted prices in active markets for identical assets and liabilities. </font></p>
</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="vertical-align: top;">
<p style="margin: 0pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;"> &nbsp; </font></p>
</td>
<td style="vertical-align: top;">
<p style="margin: 0pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;"> &nbsp; </font></p>
</td>
<td style="vertical-align: top;">
<p style="margin: 0pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;"> &nbsp; </font></p>
</td>
</tr>

</table>
<table cellspacing="0" cellpadding="0" style="border-collapse: collapse; margin-left: 0pt; width: 100%;" width="100%">

<tr>
<td style="vertical-align: top; width: 18pt;">
<p style="margin: 0pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;"> &nbsp; </font></p>
</td>
<td style="vertical-align: top; width: 18pt;">
<p style="margin: 0pt;"><font style="font-family: Symbol; font-size: 10pt;"> &#61623; </font></p>
</td>
<td style="vertical-align: top;">
<p style="margin: 0pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;"> Level <font class=" FactMarked">2</font>: Inputs include observable data points such as (i) quoted prices for similar assets or liabilities in active markets, (ii) quoted prices for identical or similar assets or liabilities in markets that are not active, and (iii) inputs (other than quoted prices) such as interest rates and yield curves that are directly or indirectly observable for the asset or liability. </font></p>

<p style="background-color: #ffffff; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">The Company amortizes the intangible assets related to developed technology, patents and trademarks using the straight-line method over the estimated useful lives of the assets, which range from <font class="TaggedFact">five</font> to <font class="TaggedFact">ten</font> years. Total amortization expense was $<font class="TaggedFact">886,000</font> and $<font class="TaggedFact">612,000</font> for the years ended October 31, 2016 and 2015, respectively. Following the annual review for impairment, an impairment charge <font>of $<font class="TaggedFact">298,000</font> w</font>as included in amortization expense for the year ended October 31, 2016 in relation to the full impairment of two acquired patents and in-process research and development assets that were abandoned or for which future revenue and cash flow could not be forecasted within the Company's strategic efforts. Of the total, amortization expense related to software costs of $<font class="TaggedFact">336,000</font> and $<font class="TaggedFact">379,000</font> is included in cost of equipment, supplies and accessories revenues for the years ended October 31, 2016 and 2015, respectively. Amortization expense classified in cost of equipment, supplies and accessories revenue for the years ended October 31, 2016 and 2015 includes<font>&nbsp;$<font class="TaggedFact">245,000</font></font>&nbsp;and $<font class="TaggedFact">266,000</font>, respectively, of software development costs that were written off to fully impair two software products that were deemed to have no future value.</font></p>

<p style="margin: 0pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="background-color: #ffffff; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">Sales of the Company&#8217;s equipment are subject to a warranty obligation. Equipment warranties typically extend for a period of <font class="TaggedFact">twelve</font> months from the date of installation. Standard warranty terms are included in customer contracts. Under the terms of these warranties, the Company is obligated to repair or replace any components or assemblies that it deems defective in workmanship or materials. The Company reserves the right to reject warranty claims if it determines that failure is due to normal wear, customer modifications, improper maintenance or misuse. The Company maintains a warranty reserve that reflects the estimated expenses it will incur to honor the warranties on its products. The Company adjusts the warranty reserve based on the number and type of equipment subject to warranty and the remaining months of warranty coverage. The warranty reserve adjustment reflects the Company&#8217;s historical warranty experience based on the type of equipment.</font>&nbsp;</p>

<p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;"><br></p>

<td style="vertical-align: top; width: 36pt;">
<p style="margin: 0pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-weight: bold;"> (9) </font></p>
</td>
<td style="vertical-align: top;">
<p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-weight: bold;"> Financing Arrangements </font></p>
</td>
</tr>

</table>
<p style="margin: 0pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">On July 24, 2014, the Company entered into a credit agreement (&#8220;Agreement&#8221;) with BMO Harris Bank NA (&#8220;Bank&#8221;).</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">The Agreement, as amended, included a $<font class="TaggedFact">4.0</font> million term loan and $<font class="TaggedFact">250,000</font> revolving credit facility, which was also available for standby and commercial letters of credit. The term loan, which bore&nbsp;interest at a floating rate, was payable in equal monthly principal installments of $<font class="TaggedFact">66,667</font> over a <font class="TaggedFact">five</font>-year period commencing August 31, 2014 and was evidenced by a term note. The Company funded the original $<font class=" FactMarked">4.0</font> million under the term loan on July 24, 2014. The Company used these proceeds in connection with its acquisition of Medisoft SA. The revolving credit facility had a <font class="TaggedFact">one</font>-year term, which had been renewed through July 31, 2016. The Company could&nbsp;use the revolving credit facility from time to time for working capital or general corporate needs. The revolving credit facility was evidenced by a revolving note. </font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;"><br></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;"><font style="font-family: 'times new roman', times; font-size: 10pt;">On June 14, 2016, the Company paid off the remaining balance of the term loan and terminated the revolving credit facility.</font><br></p>
</div>
<p align="justify" style="margin: 0px; clear: left; font-family: 'times new roman'; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</p><div class="TaggedFact">
<div>
<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin-top: 0; margin-bottom: 0pt; margin-left: 0in; text-indent: 0in; text-align: justify;"><b>(10) &nbsp; &nbsp; &nbsp; &nbsp; Shareholders&#8217; Equity</b></p>
</div>
<p style="margin: 0pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="background-color: #ffffff; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-style: italic; font-weight: bold;">Stock Options, Restricted Stock Awards and Other Stock-based Compensation</font></p>
<p style="background-color: #ffffff; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="background-color: #ffffff; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">At a Special Meeting of Shareholders held on August 22, 2007, the shareholders approved the MGC Diagnostics Corporation 2007 Stock Incentive Plan (the &#8220;2007 Plan&#8221;) and reserved <font class="TaggedFact">250,000</font> shares of its common stock for issuance under the 2007 Plan. The 2007 Plan has been amended several times and currently authorizes the issuance of up to <font class="TaggedFact">1,150,000</font> shares under various incentive forms. As of October 31, 2016, stock options for <font class="TaggedFact">371,733</font> shares were outstanding, <font class="TaggedFact">81,157</font>&nbsp;shares had been issued upon exercise of stock options, <font class="TaggedFact">404,857</font>&nbsp;shares had been issued pursuant to fully vested restricted stock awards, <font class="TaggedFact">10,221</font>&nbsp;shares had been issued as performance share awards, <font class="TaggedFact">19,906</font>&nbsp;shares were issued in lieu of Director regular cash retainer fees, <font class="TaggedFact">41,497</font>&nbsp;shares were subject to unvested restricted stock awards and <font class="TaggedFact">220,629</font>&nbsp;shares were available for future grant in some form. Under the terms of the 2007 Plan, as amended, up to 1,150,000 shares may be issued pursuant to incentive stock awards, up to <font class="TaggedFact">650,000</font> may be issued as incentives for non-employee directors and up to <font class="TaggedFact">650,000</font> may be issued pursuant to restricted stock grants. As of October 31, 2016, these sub-limits permit a maximum of <font class="TaggedFact">203,646</font>&nbsp;additional restricted stock awards to be issued.</font></p>
<p style="background-color: #ffffff; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">The 2007 Plan provides that incentive stock options and nonqualified stock options to purchase shares of common stock may be granted at prices determined by the Compensation Committee, except that the purchase price of incentive stock options may not be less than the fair market value of the stock at the date of grant. Options under the plan are subject to vesting schedules established on the date of grant. In addition, the 2007 Plan allows the granting of restricted stock awards, stock appreciation rights and performance stock.</font></p>

The Company issues new shares when stock options are exercised. Unrecognized compensation expense related to outstanding stock options as of October 31, 2016 was $<font class="TaggedFact">701,000</font> and is expected to be recognized over a weighted average period of <font class="TaggedFact">1.94</font> years.</font></p>

<p style="background-color: #ffffff; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;">&nbsp;</p>
<p style="margin: 0pt; text-indent: 34.2pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-style: italic; font-weight: bold;">Valuation Assumptions</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt; text-indent: 34.2pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt; text-indent: 34.2pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">The Company uses the Black-Scholes option-pricing model (&#8220;Black-Scholes model&#8221;) to determine the fair value of stock options as of the grant date. The fair value of stock options under the Black-Scholes model requires management to make assumptions regarding projected employee stock option exercise behaviors, risk-free interest rates, volatility of the Company&#8217;s stock price and expected dividends. The expense recognized for options granted under the 2007 Plan is equal to the fair value of stock options as of the grant date. The following table provides the weighted average fair value of options granted to employees and the related assumptions used in the Black-Scholes model for stock option grants made during the two years ended <font>October 31, 2016</font>:</font></p>

<p style="margin: 0pt; text-indent: 34.2pt;"><font style="background-color: #ffffff;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-style: italic; font-weight: bold;">Restricted Stock Awards</font><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-style: italic; font-weight: bold;">&nbsp;</font></font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt; text-indent: 34.2pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt; text-indent: 34.2pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">Restricted stock awards are awards of common stock that are subject to restrictions on transfer and to a risk of forfeiture if the holder leaves the Company before the restrictions lapse. The holder of a restricted stock award is generally entitled at all times on and after the date of issuance of the restricted shares to exercise the rights of a shareholder of the Company, including the right to vote the shares. The value of stock awards that vest over time was established by the market price on the date of its grant. A summary of the Company&#8217;s restricted stock activity for the years ended October 31, 2016 and 2015 is presented in the following table:</font></p>

<p style="margin: 0pt; text-indent: 34.2pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">Unrecognized compensation expense related to outstanding restricted stock awards to employees and directors as of October 31, 2016 was $<font class="TaggedFact">124,000</font> and is expected to be recognized over a weighted average period of <font class="TaggedFact">0.59</font>&nbsp;years.</font>&nbsp;</p>
<p style="margin: 0pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt; text-indent: 34.2pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-style: italic; font-weight: bold;">Director Stock Awards in Lieu of Cash Retainer Fees</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt; text-indent: 34.2pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</font><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt; text-indent: 34.2pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">The Company offers&nbsp;a program that allows non-employee Board members to elect and receive shares from the 2007 Plan in lieu of some or all of their quarterly cash retainer fees. During the year ended October 31, 2016 and 2015, the Company issued <font class="TaggedFact">7,099</font>&nbsp;and <font class="TaggedFact">7,057</font>&nbsp;shares, respectively, under this program. The expense was recognized at the time of share issuance and totaled $<font class="TaggedFact">45,000</font> in both of the years ended October 31, 2016 and 2015.</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt; text-indent: 34.2pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</font><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt; text-indent: 34.2pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-style: italic; font-weight: bold;">Employee Stock Purchase Plan</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt; text-indent: 34.2pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</font><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt; text-indent: 34.2pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">The MGC Diagnostics Corporation 2003 Employee Stock Purchase Plan, as amended (&#8220;Purchase Plan&#8221;), allows participating employees to purchase up to <font class="TaggedFact">200,000</font> shares of the Company&#8217;s common stock at a discount through payroll deductions. The Purchase Plan is available to all employees subject to eligibility requirements. Under the Purchase Plan, participating employees may purchase the Company&#8217;s common stock on a voluntary after-tax basis at a price that is the lower of <font class="TaggedFact">85</font>% of the fair market value of one share of common stock at the beginning or end of each stock purchase phase. The Purchase Plan is carried out in six-month phases, with phases beginning on January 1 and July 1 of each calendar year. For the phases that ended on December 31, 2015 and June 30, 2016, employees purchased <font class="TaggedFact">11,248</font>&nbsp;and <font class="TaggedFact">8,481</font> shares at prices of $<font class="TaggedFact">4.47</font>&nbsp;and $<font class="TaggedFact">5.54</font>&nbsp;per share, respectively. &nbsp;<font style="color: #000000; text-indent: 45.6px; text-transform: none; white-space: normal; widows: 2; word-spacing: 0px; -webkit-text-stroke-width: 0px; background-color: #ffffff; display: inline !important; float: none;">For the phases that ended on December 31, 2014 and June 30, 2015, employees purchased </font><font class="TaggedFact">12,040</font><font style="color: #000000; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 13.3333px; font-style: normal; font-variant-ligatures: normal; font-variant-caps: normal; font-weight: normal; letter-spacing: normal; orphans: 2; text-align: start; text-indent: 45.6px; text-transform: none; white-space: normal; widows: 2; word-spacing: 0px; -webkit-text-stroke-width: 0px; background-color: #ffffff; display: inline !important; float: none;"> and </font><font class="TaggedFact">11,711</font><font style="color: #000000; <p style="margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-style: italic; font-weight: bold;">Tax Impact of Stock-Based Compensation</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</font><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt; text-indent: 34.55pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">The Company reports the benefit of tax deductions in excess of recognized stock-based compensation expense on the consolidated statements of cash flows as operating&nbsp;cash flows. For the years ended October 31, 2016 and 2015, there were no excess tax benefits realized due to the U.S. federal valuation allowance against deferred tax asset recognition of available deductions.</font></p>

<p style="margin: 0pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</font><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt; text-indent: 34.2pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">The Company leases domestic office and manufacturing space, and various office accessories. The building lease for the Company&#8217;s present domestic office and manufacturing space expires on December 31, 2017. The Company also leases office and manufacturing space in France and Italy, which leases expire at various dates through <font class="TaggedFact">December 31, 2020</font> and auto leases through 2021. Total lease expenses, including office and manufacturing spaces, autos and office accessories, were $<font class="TaggedFact">460,000</font> and $<font class="TaggedFact">458,000</font> for the years ended October 31, 2016 and 2015, respectively.</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt; text-indent: 34.2pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</font><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt; text-indent: 34.2pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">The renewal terms of the building lease for the Company&#8217;s domestic office and manufacturing facility include rental payments that escalate annually at stated amounts. The lessor also agreed to make certain leasehold improvements in the early portion of the renewal period. The Company uses deferred rental liability accounts to accrue the combined effect of the future payments in relation to the lessor-funded improvements and the normal rent expense for each year, calculated as the average of the <font class=" FactMarked">five</font>-year committed payments. At October 31, 2013, the Company recorded $<font class="TaggedFact">210,000</font> of the estimated lessor-funded leasehold improvements, with additional improvements similarly funded totaling $<font class="TaggedFact">51,000</font>&nbsp;and $<font class="TaggedFact">33,000</font>&nbsp;completed in the years ended October 31, 2016 and 2015, respectively. The balance of the remaining lessor-funded leasehold improvements will be recorded when completed. Future minimum lease payments under operating leases in effect as of October 31, 2016 are as follows:</font></p>

<td style="background-color: #ffffff; border-bottom-color: #000000; border-bottom-style: double; border-bottom-width: 2.25pt; vertical-align: bottom; border-top-width: 1pt; border-top-style: solid; border-top-color: #000000;">

<p align="justify" style="margin: 0px; clear: left; font-family: 'times new roman'; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</p><div class="TaggedFact">
<p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-weight: bold;">(12)</font><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-weight: bold;">&nbsp;</font><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-weight: bold;">&nbsp;</font><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-weight: bold;">&nbsp;</font><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-weight: bold;">&nbsp;</font><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-weight: bold;">&nbsp;&nbsp;</font><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-weight: bold;">&nbsp;</font><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-weight: bold;">&nbsp;</font><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-weight: bold;">Income Taxes</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-weight: bold;">&nbsp;</font><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-weight: bold;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt; text-indent: 34.2pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">The<font> Company recorded a net income tax provision&nbsp;of $923,000 for the fiscal year ended October 31, 2016 compared to an income tax benefit of $<font class=" FactMarked">3,549,000</font> for fiscal year ended October 31, 2015. The fiscal 2016 income tax expense includes U.S. deferred expense of approximately $593,000, foreign deferred expense of approximately $106,000 and U.S. current tax of $205,000 including state taxes, minimum fees&nbsp;and federal alternative minimum tax ("AMT"), foreign current provincial tax expenses of $1,000 and an increase in the reserve for uncertain tax positions total<font>ing $31,000,</font> of which $18,000 was included as a component of income tax expense. The fiscal 2015&nbsp;benefit includes a tax benefit of approximately $<font class="NegatedFact">3,111,000</font> as result of the Company reversing a substantial portion of the valuation allowance on its domestic deferred tax assets&nbsp;in addition to approximately $<font class=" FactMarked">544,000</font> of foreign deferred income tax benefit recorded related to Medisoft Belgium. These tax benefits were partially offset by current estimated federal AMT, state tax expense, minimum fees, and provincial tax expense totaling $<font class="TaggedFact">106,000</font>&nbsp;for fiscal 2015.</font></font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt; text-indent: 34.2pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</font><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt; text-indent: 34.2pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">The Company has federal net operating loss (&#8220;NOL&#8221;) and general business tax credit carry forwards; however, the utilization of some of these tax loss and tax credit carry forwards is limited under Internal Revenue Code (&#8220;IRC&#8221;) &#167;382 and &#167;383, respectively, as a result of a IRS-deemed change in ownership that occurred in the fourth quarter of fiscal 2006. The Company estimates that the amount of federal NOL carry forward at October 31, 2016 that is not limited is approximately $<font class="TaggedFact">6.5</font>&nbsp;million. These loss carry forwards will expire in years 2018 through 2032. None of the current loss carry forward benefits expire until 2018 after considering the statutory limitations described above. Additionally, the Company has concluded that all general business credit carry forwards generated prior to the 2006 change in ownership are limited and not available for use in future years. The Company also has federal and state combined general business credits of $<font class="TaggedFact">461,000</font>, which will carry forward and begin to expire in 2033. Usage of this general business credit carry forward is not limited because it was generated after the change in ownership. The Company also has $<font class="TaggedFact">266,000</font> of alternative minimum tax credit carry forwards that do not expire. The alternative minimum tax credit carry forward benefits are limited by IRC &#167;383 but their ultimate use is not affected since these do not expire. The Company also has combined foreign NOLs of approximately $<font class="TaggedFact">4.8</font>&nbsp;million. Foreign NOL expiration varies by country; however a substantial portion of the foreign NOLs are in Belgium which do not expire.</font></p>

<p style="margin: 0pt; text-indent: 34.2pt;"><br></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt; text-indent: 34.2pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">The valuation allo<font>wance for deferred tax assets as of October 31, 2016 and 2015&nbsp;was $<font class=" FactMarked">2,723,000</font>&nbsp;and $<font class=" FactMarked">963,000</font>, respectively. The total valuation allowance increased by $<font class="NegatedFact">1,760,000</font>&nbsp;for the year ended October 31, 2016 due to the adoption of ASU 2016-09 and additional valuation allowance recorded against Belgium deferred tax assets and other foreign provision to return adjustments.</font></font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt; text-indent: 34.2pt;">&nbsp;<br></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt; text-indent: 34.2pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">In assessing the need for a valuation allowance, management considers whether it is more likely than not that some portion or all of the deferred tax assets will not be realized. Management considers the scheduled reversal of deferred tax liabilities, projected future taxable income and tax planning strategies in making this assessment. The ultimate realization of deferred tax assets is dependent upon the generation of future taxable income. Based on the Company&#8217;s assessment of all available evidence including (i) previous <font class="TaggedFact">three</font>-year cumulative income before infrequent and unusual items, (ii) a history of generating income before taxes for the past <font class="TaggedFact">three</font>&nbsp;years and (iii) estimates of future Company profitability. During the third quarter of fiscal year 2015, the Company incurred a non-cash benefit of approximately $3,111,000 due to the reversal of a substantial portion of the valuation allowance on the Company&#8217;s domestic deferred tax assets, based on its determination that a portion of its domestic deferred tax assets would more likely than not be realized.</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt; text-indent: 34.2pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt; text-indent: 34.2pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">In&nbsp;March 2016, the FASB issued ASU No. 2016-09, which simplifies various aspects of accounting for share-based payments to employees. Key provisions of the new standard include requiring excess tax benefits and shortfalls to be recorded as income tax benefit or expense in the income statement, rather than in equity, and permitting an election to record the impact of pre-vesting forfeitures as they occur. &nbsp;The new guidance is effective for fiscal years beginning after December 15, 2016, and interim periods within those fiscal years, with early adoption permitted. The Company elected to early adopt ASU 2016-09 during the quarter ended October 31, 2016, retroactive to November 1, 2015. &nbsp;The adoption of ASU 2016-09 required no retrospective adjustment to the consolidated financial statements. The adoptio<font>n resulted in the addition at recognition of $<font class="TaggedFact">2,824,000</font> in net operating loss ("NOL") carryforwards from excess tax benefits previously unrecorded in the consolidated financial statements. The additional NOL carryforwards resulted in an increase in the gross&nbsp;deferred tax assets of approximately $<font class="TaggedFact">960,000</font>, however, these NOLs are subject to a valuation allowance due to the Company only releasing a portion of its valuation allowance for domestic deferred tax assets in the prior year. Consequently, there was no income tax expense or benefit impact or adjustment to reta</font>ined earnings during the year from the adoption.</font></p>

<p style="margin: 0pt; text-indent: 34.2pt;"><br></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt; text-indent: 34.2pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">In accounting for uncertainty in income taxes, we recognize the financial statement benefit of a tax position only after determining that the relevant tax authority would more likely than not sustain the position following an audit. For tax positions meeting the more likely than not threshold, the amount recognized in the financial statements is the largest benefit that has a greater than 50% likelihood of being realized upon ultimate settlement with the relevant tax authority. The Company recognizes interest and penalties on any unrecognized tax benefits as a component of income tax expense. For the years ended October 31, 2016 and 2015, the liability for uncertainties in income taxes increased by $<font class="TaggedFact">31,000</font> and $<font class="TaggedFact">4,000</font>, respectively. The Company does not expect the amount of reserves for uncertain tax positions to change significantly in the next twelve months.</font></p>

<p style="margin: 0pt; text-indent: 34.2pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt; text-indent: 34.2pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">If recognized, approximately $<font class="TaggedFact">59,000</font> of these benefits would lower the effective tax rate. The remaining $<font class="TaggedFact">33,000</font> if recognized would result in a deferred tax asset subject to a valuation allowance and therefore not affect the effective rate. The unrecognized tax benefits are related to potential state income tax liabilities in prior years including interest as well as research and development credits.</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt; text-indent: 34.2pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt; text-indent: 34.2pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">The Company is subject to income taxes in the U.S. federal and various state and international jurisdictions. With few exceptions, the Company is no longer subject to U.S. federal and state income tax examinations by tax authorities for years ending prior to 1998. We are generally subject to U.S. federal and state examinations for all tax years since 1998 due to our net operating loss carryforwards and utilization of the carryforwards in years still open under statute. The expiration of the statute of limitations related to the various state income tax returns that the Company file varies by state. There is no statute of limitations for assessments related to jurisdictions where the Company may have a nexus but has chosen not to file an income tax return. The expiration of the statute of limitations related to foreign jurisdictions varies by country.</font></p>

<p align="justify" style="margin: 0px; clear: left; font-family: 'times new roman'; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</p><div class="TaggedFact">
<p style="margin: 0pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-weight: bold;">(13)</font><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-weight: bold;">&nbsp;</font><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-weight: bold;">&nbsp;</font><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-weight: bold;">&nbsp;</font><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-weight: bold;">&nbsp;</font><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-weight: bold;">&nbsp;</font><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-weight: bold;">&nbsp;</font><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-weight: bold;">&nbsp;</font><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-weight: bold;">&nbsp;</font><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-weight: bold;">401(k) Savings Plan</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt; text-indent: 34.2pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">Substantially all domestic employees are eligible to participate in the 401(k) Savings Plan (&#8220;Savings Plan&#8221;). Employees may make pre-tax voluntary contributions to their individual accounts up to a maximum of <font class="TaggedFact">50</font>% of their aggregate compensation, but not more than currently allowable limits established by the Internal Revenue Service. The Savings Plan permits matching and discretionary employer contributions. The Company matches <font class="TaggedFact">50</font>% of the first <font class="TaggedFact">6</font>% of an employee&#8217;s annual compensation. Company contributions to the Savings Plan were $<font class="TaggedFact">243,000</font> and $<font class="TaggedFact">230,000</font> for the years ended October 31, 2016 and 2015, respectively.</font></p>
</div>
<p align="justify" style="margin: 0px; clear: left; font-family: 'times new roman'; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</p><div class="TaggedFact">
<p style="margin: 0pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-weight: bold;">(14)</font><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-weight: bold;">&nbsp;</font><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-weight: bold;">&nbsp;</font><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-weight: bold;">&nbsp;</font><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-weight: bold;">&nbsp;</font><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-weight: bold;">&nbsp;</font><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-weight: bold;">&nbsp;</font><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-weight: bold;">&nbsp;</font><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-weight: bold;">&nbsp;</font><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-weight: bold;">Segment Reporting</font></p>

<p align="justify" style="margin: 0px; clear: left; font-family: 'times new roman'; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</p><div class="TaggedFact">
<p style="margin: 0pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-weight: bold;">(15)</font><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-weight: bold;">&nbsp;</font><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-weight: bold;">&nbsp;</font><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-weight: bold;">&nbsp;</font><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-weight: bold;">&nbsp;</font><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-weight: bold;">&nbsp;</font><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-weight: bold;">&nbsp;</font><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-weight: bold;">&nbsp;</font><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-weight: bold;">&nbsp;</font><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-weight: bold;">Litigation</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt; text-indent: 34.2pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">The Company is also subject to certain claims and lawsuits that have been filed in the ordinary course of business. From time to time, the Company initiates lawsuits against others to enforce patents or to seek collection of debts in the ordinary course of business. The Company is not subject to any pending litigation except as set forth below.</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt; text-indent: 34.2pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-weight: bold;">MGC Diagnostics Corporation v. Mr. Guy Martinot and Dr. Jean-Beno&#238;t Martinot</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">In November 2015, the Company commenced litigation in the French-speaking courts of Brussels, Belgium against the selling shareholders of Medisoft for violations of representations and warranties in the stock purchase agreement dated as of July 10, 2014 under which the Company purchased Medisoft. The C</font><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">ompany alleged that these violations resulted in Company damages of approximately &#8364;<font class="TaggedFact">985,400</font> ($<font class="TaggedFact">1,084,000</font>)<font>.</font> In May 2015, the Company received payment of &#8364;<font class="TaggedFact">406,700</font> ($<font class="TaggedFact">447,000</font>) with respect to these alleged violations pursuant to a bank guaranteed contractual esc</font><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">row fund and has reflected that payment on its books and records.<font style="font-size: 10.0pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman','serif'; mso-fareast-font-family: 'Times New Roman'; mso-ansi-language: EN-US; mso-fareast-language: EN-US; mso-bidi-language: AR-SA;">&nbsp;On May 30, 2016, the defendant selling shareholders filed an answer to dispute all claims and asserted a counterclaim against the Company seeking to recover the &#8364;406,700 that was paid to the Company in May 2015 and legal costs. <font style="font-size: 10.0pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman','serif'; mso-fareast-font-family: 'Times New Roman'; mso-ansi-language: EN-US; mso-fareast-language: EN-US; mso-bidi-language: AR-SA;">The Company continues to believe the Medisoft selling shareholders are liable to it for violations of representations and warranties in the stock purchase agreement and intends to continue to pursue this matter. </font> </font>The Company has not accrued any losses related to the litigation or accrued any related legal costs it has not yet incurred. The Company currently expects that this litigation process may continue until the fall of 2017.</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-weight: bold; background-color: #ffffff;">Neurovirtual USA, Inc. v. MGC Diagnostics Corporation</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; background-color: #ffffff;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; background-color: #ffffff;">On January 12, 2016, Neurovirtual USA, Inc. commenced a lawsuit against the Company in the United States District Court for the Southern District of New York asserting breach of contract, anticipatory breach of contract, and fraud in the inducement. Neurovirtual commenced the lawsuit after MGC, in a letter dated December 17, 2015, informed Neurovirtual that MGC was rescinding a distribution agreement dated March 31, 2014 between Neurovirtual and MGC because, among things, Neurovirtual failed to comply with applicable Minnesota law in connection with the distribution agreement. Neurovirtual alleged (i) damages of <font class="TaggedFact">$1,055,120</font> for breach of contract, (ii) damages of <font class="TaggedFact">$1,363,850</font> for anticipatory breach of contract; and (iii) damages of no less than <font class="TaggedFact">$5.0</font> million for fraud in the inducement. MGC believed that its rescission of the distribution agreement was proper and that it had&nbsp;valid defenses to the Neurovirtual claims.</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;"><br></p>
<p style="margin: 0in 0in 0.0001pt; text-indent: 36pt; /* font-size: 12pt; */font-family: 'Times New Roman', serif;"><font style="background-color: #ffffff;"><font style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'times new roman', times;" class="selected">The Company entered into a settlement agreement on June 14, 2016 and&nbsp;made&nbsp;a one-time cash payment of $<font class="TaggedFact">650,000</font> to Neurovirtual. &nbsp;Each party agreed to dismiss with prejudice the lawsuit and all claims against the other party. As part of the settlement, the Company has&nbsp;retained Neurovirtual sleep diagnostics inventory that it purchased and Neurovirtual will continue to support this inventory pursuant to the distribution agreement. The Company has no continuing obligation to purchase additional Neurovirtual diagnostics products. </font></font></p>
<p style="margin: 0in 0in 0.0001pt; text-indent: 34.2pt; font-size: 12pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', serif;"><br></p>
<p style="margin: 0in 0in 0.0001pt; text-indent: 36pt; /* font-size: 12pt; */font-family: 'Times New Roman', serif;"><font style="background-color: #ffffff;"><font style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'times new roman', times;" class="selected">The Company recorded&nbsp;a loss of $<font class="NegatedFact">650,000</font>,&nbsp;which is included in&nbsp;general and administrative expense for&nbsp;the year&nbsp;ended October&nbsp;31, 2016. The Company recorded a loss on&nbsp;impairment with respect to a portion of this inventory of $<font class="TaggedFact">354,000</font> in the quarter ended October 31, 2016 resulting from its ongoing analysis of projected unit sales in future periods, as adjusted at that time. The Company continues to carry inventory and other noncurrent assets as of October 31, 2016 valued at $<font class="TaggedFact">64,000</font> and $<font class="TaggedFact">115,000</font>, respectively.&nbsp;</font></font></p>
</div>

<p align="justify" style="margin: 0px; clear: left; font-family: 'times new roman'; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</p>

The dividend will b</font>e&nbsp;paid on </font><font style="border: 0px; margin: 0px; padding: 0px; box-sizing: border-box; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-style: normal; font-variant-ligatures: normal; font-variant-caps: normal; font-weight: normal; letter-spacing: normal; orphans: 2; text-align: start; text-indent: 48px; text-transform: none; white-space: normal; widows: 2; word-spacing: 0px; -webkit-text-stroke-width: 0px; color: #000000; font-size: 13.3333px; background-color: #ffffff; float: none; display: inline !important;">February 24, 2017 to holders of record as of</font><font style="border: 0px; margin: 0px; padding: 0px; box-sizing: border-box; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-style: normal; font-variant-ligatures: normal; font-variant-caps: normal; font-weight: normal; letter-spacing: normal; orphans: 2; text-align: start; text-indent: 48px; text-transform: none; white-space: normal; widows: 2; word-spacing: 0px; -webkit-text-stroke-width: 0px; color: #000000; font-size: 13.3333px; background-color: #ffffff; float: none; display: inline !important;">&nbsp;February 10, 2017.</font></font></p>

<p align="justify" style="margin: 0px; clear: left; font-family: 'times new roman'; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</p><p style="margin: 0pt;"><font style="text-decoration: underline;"><font style="color: #000000;"><a style="text-decoration: none; color: #000000; cursor: default; outline: none;" href="#" name="14_SI42HTV9WGKW4CW8SGCSW08WK80404" class="customBookmark"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 12pt; font-weight: bold;">Item 9. Changes in and Disagreements With Accountants on Accounting and Financial Disclosure.</font></a></font></font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: center;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">During the two most recent fiscal years, there were no disagreements between us and our independent registered public accounting firm on any matter of accounting principles or practices, financial statement disclosure, or auditing scope or procedure, which would have caused them to make reference thereto in their report on the consolidated financial statements for such fiscal years.</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt;"><font style="text-decoration: underline;"><font style="color: #000000;"><a style="text-decoration: none; color: #000000; cursor: default; outline: none;" href="#" name="15_43BOAZ3DKGSKCW0KCOO4GSSOO4O800" class="customBookmark"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 12pt; font-weight: bold;">Item 9A. Controls and Procedures.</font></a></font></font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-style: italic;">(a) Evaluation of Disclosure Controls and Procedures</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;"><font style="font-family: 'times new roman', times;"><font style="font-size: 10pt;">The Company maintains disclosure controls and procedures (as defined in Rules</font><font style="font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</font><font style="font-size: 10pt;">13a-15(e) and 15d-15(e) under the Securities Exchange Act of 1934) that are designed to ensure that information required to be disclosed by the Company in reports that it files or submits under the Exchange Act is (i) recorded, processed, summarized and reported within the time periods specified in SEC rules and forms and (ii) accumulated and communicated to the Company&#8217;s management, including its principal executive officer and principal financial officer, as appropriate to allow timely decisions regarding required disclosure.&nbsp;</font><font style="font-size: 10pt;">In connection with the filing of this Form 10-K, management evaluated, under the supervision and with the participation of the Company&#8217;s Chief Executive Officer (CEO), Todd M. Austin, and Chief Financial Officer (CFO), Wesley W. Winnekins, the effectiveness of the design and operation of the Co</font><font style="font-size: 10pt;">mpany&#8217;s disclosure controls and procedures as of October 31, 2016.&nbsp;Based on this assessment, management identified a material weakness in our internal control over financial reporting as described below. As a result of this material weakness, management concluded that, as of October 31, 2016, our internal control over financial reporting was not effective based on the <i style="mso-bidi-font-style: normal;">Internal Control &#8211; Integrated Framework (2013)</i> issued by the Committee of Sponsoring Organizations of the Treadway Commission (the &#8220;Framework&#8221;). </font></font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;"><br></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt;"><font style="font-family: 'times new roman', times; font-size: 10pt; font-style: italic;">(b)&nbsp;Management Report on Internal Control over Financial Reporting</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt;"><br></p>
<p style="margin: 0in 0in 0.0001pt; text-indent: 0.5in; font-size: 12pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', serif; line-height: 1;"><font style="font-family: 'times new roman', times; font-size: 10pt;">The Company&#8217;s management is responsible for establishing and maintaining adequate internal control over financial reporting, as that term is defined in Rule 13a-15(f) and 15d-15(f) of the Securities Exchange Act.<font style="mso-spacerun: yes;">&nbsp; </font>Under the supervision and with the participation of the Company&#8217;s management, including the CEO and CFO, the Company conducted an evaluation of the effectiveness of internal control over financial reporting based on the Framework.<font style="mso-spacerun: yes;">&nbsp; </font>Based on management&#8217;s testing and evaluation, we concluded that our internal control over financial reporting was not effective, and as a result, the three significant deficiencies, which when evaluated in aggregate, resulted in a material weakness in internal controls.<font style="mso-spacerun: yes;">&nbsp; </font><i style="mso-bidi-font-style: normal;"></i></font></p>
<p style="margin: 0in 0in 0.0001pt; font-size: 12pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', serif; line-height: 1;"><font style="font-family: 'times new roman', times; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0in 0in 0.0001pt; font-size: 12pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', serif; line-height: 1;"><font style="font-family: 'times new roman', times; font-size: 10pt;"><font style="mso-tab-count: 1;">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; </font>The identified material weakness arose as a result of significant deficiencies in management&#8217;s processes and controls over the development of management&#8217;s estimations of valuation reserves for allowance for doubtful accounts and inventory valuation reserves that occurred&nbsp;during the fourth quarter of 2016:<font style="mso-spacerun: yes;">&nbsp; </font></font></p>
<p style="margin: 0in 0in 0.0001pt; font-size: 12pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', serif; line-height: 1;"><font style="font-family: 'times new roman', times; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0in 0in 6pt 0.5in; text-indent: -0.25in; font-size: 12pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', serif; line-height: 1;"><font style="font-family: 'times new roman', times; font-size: 10pt;"><font style="mso-list: Ignore;">1.<font style="font-style: normal; font-variant: normal; font-weight: normal; font-stretch: normal; line-height: normal;">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; </font></font><font>We concluded that controls surrounding the gathering, interpretation and evaluation of supporting documentation for SleepVirtual sales forecasts were ineffective in determining the appropriate value of the SleepVirtual inventory on hand.<font style="mso-spacerun: yes;">&nbsp; </font></font></font></p>
<p style="margin: 0in 0in 6pt 0.5in; text-indent: -0.25in; font-size: 12pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', serif; line-height: 1;"><font style="font-family: 'times new roman', times; font-size: 10pt;"><font style="mso-list: Ignore;">2.<font style="font-style: normal; font-variant: normal; font-weight: normal; font-stretch: normal; line-height: normal;">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; </font></font>We concluded that Company policies and procedures in place surrounding demonstration inventory were not adequately followed or reviewed to ensure the demonstration inventory units were monitored for the amount of time they were deployed for selling activities.<font style="mso-spacerun: yes;">&nbsp; </font>The aging of some units required an inventory valuation reserve to properly reflect the estimated net realizable value of the demonstration units in inventory.<font style="mso-spacerun: yes;">&nbsp; </font></font></p>
<p style="margin: 0in 0in 0in 0.5in; text-indent: -0.25in; font-size: 12pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', serif; line-height: 1;"><font style="font-family: 'times new roman', times; font-size: 10pt;"><font style="mso-list: Ignore;">3.<font style="font-style: normal; font-variant: normal; font-weight: normal; font-stretch: normal; line-height: normal;">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; </font></font>We concluded that the controls surrounding estimation of collectability of aged international accounts receivable were not adequate to establish the correct reserve for a specific customer as of October 31, 2016.<font style="mso-spacerun: yes;">&nbsp; </font></font></p>
<p style="margin: 0in 0in 0.0001pt; font-size: 12pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', serif; line-height: 1;"><font style="font-family: 'times new roman', times; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0in 0in 0.0001pt; text-indent: 0.5in; font-size: 12pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', serif; line-height: 1;"><font style="font-family: 'times new roman', times; font-size: 10pt;">The material weakness resulted in misstatements in the recorded amount of inventory valuation reserves and allowance for doubtful accounts reserves that were corrected in the fourth quarter of 2016 prior to issuance of the Company&#8217;s consolidated financial statements.<font style="mso-spacerun: yes;">&nbsp; </font>We concluded that a reasonable possibility existed that a material misstatement in the Company&#8217;s consolidated financial statements would not have been prevented or detected on a timely basis.</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0in 0in 0.0001pt; font-size: 12pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', serif; line-height: 1;"><font style="font-family: 'times new roman', times; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;"><br></p>

<p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: left;"><font style="font-family: 'times new roman', times;"><strong><font style="font-size: 10pt;"><font>Remediation Plan for Material</font> Weaknesses in Internal Control over Financial Reporting</font></strong></font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt; text-align: left;"><strong></strong><br></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt; text-align: left;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">During our 2017 fiscal quarter beginning February 1, 2017, we intend to&nbsp;implement the following remediation plan to address the material weakness describe above:</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt; text-align: left;"><br></p>

<p style="margin: 0pt;"><font style="font-family: 'times new roman', times; font-size: 10pt; font-style: italic;">(c)&nbsp;Inherent Limitations on Control Systems</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt;"><br></p>
<p style="margin: 0in 0in 0.0001pt; text-indent: 0.5in; font-size: 12pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', serif; line-height: 1;"><font style="font-family: 'times new roman', times; font-size: 10pt;">Because of the inherent limitations in all control systems, no evaluation of controls can provide absolute assurance that all control issues and instances of fraud, if any, will be or have been detected.<font style="mso-spacerun: yes;">&nbsp; </font>These inherent limitations include the realities that judgments in decision-making can be faulty, and that breakdowns can occur because of simple error or mistake.<font style="mso-spacerun: yes;">&nbsp; </font>Additionally, controls can be circumvented by the individual acts of some persons, by collusion of two or more people, or by management override of the control.<font style="mso-spacerun: yes;">&nbsp; </font>The design of any system of controls also is based in part upon certain assumptions about the likelihood of future events and there can be no assurance that any design will succeed in achieving its stated goals under all potential future conditions; over time, controls may become inadequate because of changes in conditions, or the degree of compliance with the policies or procedures may deteriorate.</font><br></p>
<p style="margin: 0in 0in 0.0001pt; text-indent: 0.5in; font-size: 12pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', serif; line-height: 1;"><br></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt;"><font style="font-family: 'times new roman', times; font-size: 10pt; font-style: italic;">(d) Changes in Internal&nbsp;Control</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0in 0in 0.0001pt; text-indent: 0.5in; font-size: 12pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman', serif; line-height: 1;"><br></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;"><font style="font-family: 'times new roman', times; font-size: 10pt;">There have been no changes in internal control over financial reporting that occurred during the fiscal 2016 fourth quarter that have materially affected, or are reasonably likely to materially affect, the Company&#8217;s internal control over financial reporting, except as noted above. &nbsp;The Company is taking steps to ensure that it remediates the material weakness by implementing enhanced control procedures over accounting for valuation reserve estimation practices as noted above.</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;">&nbsp;<br></p>

Security Ownership of Certain Beneficial Owners and Management and Related Stockholder Matters</font></a></font></font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;"><font style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">The information called for by Item 403 under Regulation S-K will be set forth under the captions &#8220;Security Ownership of Certain Beneficial Owners and Management and Related Stockholder Matters&#8221; in the Company&#8217;s 2017 Proxy Statement, and is incorporated herein by reference.</font></p>
